items.title: Microclimatic regulation effects of landscape elements on university campus in a temperate monsoon climate zone: A case study during extreme summer heat
items.summary: by Lei Fan, Yixin Liang, Zixian Li, Yan Zhou Although temperate monsoon climate regions are traditionally known for their harsh winter climates, the combined effects of rapid urbanization and global climate change have significantly intensified summer urban heat island effects in these areas, making them a neglected yet increasingly severe challenge in high-latitude urban climate adaptation planning. This study takes a typical campus in Shenyang, a temperate monsoon climate region in Northeast China, as the experimental subject. It quantitatively dissects the non-linear statistical associations and regulatory mechanisms of biotic and abiotic landscape elements and their spatial configurations on microclimate parameters and human thermal comfort (Physiologically Equivalent Temperature, PET) by combining microclimate field observations with validated ENVI-met numerical simulations.
items.author: Lei Fan, Yixin Liang, Zixian Li et al.

items.title: Fabrication and evaluation of a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel for the treatment of ocular bacterial infections
items.summary: by Neda Sistani Karampour, Pouya Dolati, Anayatollah Salim, Maryam Abedini Baghbadorani, Maryam Keykhaee, Somayeh Handali, Eskandar Moghimipour Topical ocular drug delivery is often restricted by rapid precorneal clearance, which can decrease drug residence time and bioavailability at the ocular surface. The purpose of the study was to develop a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel (SA-Nio-Gel) to enhance ocular drug delivery. Thin film hydration method was used for the preparation of SA niosomes, employing nonionic surfactants (Span 60 and Span 80) and cholesterol. The optimized niosomal formulation was then incorporated into a Carbopol 934 gel base to prepare the final SA-Nio-Gel formulation. The optimized niosomes exhibited encapsulation efficiency of 76% ± 1.5 and a mean particle size of 129.7 ± 2.52 nm.
items.author: Neda Sistani Karampour, Pouya Dolati, Anayatollah Salim et al.

items.title: Ensemble frequency ratio-maximum entropy landslide susceptibility modelling for climate‑resilient road corridors in Bocas del Toro and Chiriquí, Panama
items.summary: by Dereck Mbeh Petiangma, Gerald G. Singh, Enrique Williams, Jeffrey Gerardo Ramos Perez, Rachel Collin Landslides are a major rainfall-triggered hazard affecting road infrastructure across the mountainous terrain of western Panama. This study develops an ensemble Frequency Ratio (FR)-Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) modelling framework to assess landslide susceptibility, identify critical management zones, and determine key drivers of slope failure along road corridors in the mainland districts of Bocas del Toro and along the Rambala-Hornito-David route. Within a 1,000 m corridor buffer, 87 mapped landslides (63 for training and 24 for validation) and 15 environmental conditioning factors were used to develop and validate the FR and MaxEnt models.
items.author: Dereck Mbeh Petiangma, Gerald G. Singh, Enrique Williams et al.

items.title: Social jetlag and DXA-derived adiposity in Korean adults: A nationwide study using the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
items.summary: by Soojin Kim, Heewon Bae Background Social jetlag, the discrepancy between weekday and weekend sleep timing, is a behavioral marker of circadian timing mismatch and has been linked to obesity, mainly through conventional anthropometric measures. We examined its association with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived adiposity using the nationally representative 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES). Methods This cross-sectional study included adults aged ≥40 years reporting usual weekday and weekend bedtimes and wake times. Social jetlag, the absolute difference between weekday and weekend sleep midpoints, was categorized as Results Among 4,483 participants, 267 (6.0%) had social jetlag ≥2 h.
items.author: Soojin Kim, Heewon Bae

items.title: Land degradation neutrality state and progress in the Central Region, Malawi
items.summary: by Kennedy Sones Nazombe, Charles Bakolo, Brighton A. Chunga, Principal Mdolo, Jean Mtethiwa, Rodrick Mlewa, Kennedy Adamson, Devie Chilonga, Kelvin Chomanika Achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is vital for the long-term sustainability of human well-being and the realisation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.3.1. We estimated the overall indicator of SDG 15.3.1, the proportion of land that is degraded over the total land area in the Central Region, Malawi, from 2001 to 2022, using the Trends.Earth tool in QGIS. The study applied the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) Good Practice Guidance methodology for SDG Indicator 15.3.1 assessment, integrating land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon (SOC) sub-indicators.
items.author: Kennedy Sones Nazombe, Charles Bakolo, Brighton A. Chunga et al.

items.title: A lightweight vision-based framework for automated aero-engine blade damage inspection
items.summary: by Xiaobo Ning, Hang Zhao, Kang Zeng, Zhengwei Zhang Automated visual inspection of aero-engine blades is central to aviation safety, yet it is challenged by damage that is small and low-contrast against a strongly textured metal surface, and by the need for models that are light enough for edge deployment. This paper presents a lightweight vision-based framework for automated blade damage inspection. Rather than assembling independent detection modules, the framework is organized as a three-stage inspection pipeline: (1) a multi-scale feature-discrimination stage (MSBlock) captures defects across a wide size range at negligible computational cost; (2) a texture-suppression stage (TSA) filters high-frequency machining-background noise through product-based channel–spatial attention, exposing genuine defects; and (3) an efficient-prediction stage (Detect_Efficient) fuses cross-scale features and recalibrates confidence with roughly half the parameters of a standard head.
items.author: Xiaobo Ning, Hang Zhao, Kang Zeng et al.

items.title: Modeling and controlling a half-car model suspension system using an ANFIS controller
items.summary: by Sisay Ewunetie Fisha, Amanuel Gebisa Aga, Tatek Mamo Wachamo Passive suspension systems (PSS) use fixed spring and damping characteristics and cannot adapt to changing road disturbances and operating conditions. Active suspension systems (ASS) address this limitation by generating additional control forces, but controller design must balance ride comfort, road holding, model uncertainty, and control effort. This study develops a four-degree-of-freedom (4-DOF) longitudinal half-car model and evaluates an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller against PSS and PID-controlled ASS under double-bump and ISO-classified random Type A and Type C Road profiles at 10 and 20 m/s. The ANFIS controller is trained using PID-generated input-output data with two inputs, five Gaussian membership functions per input, 25 Takagi-Sugeno rules, and 150 training epochs.
items.author: Sisay Ewunetie Fisha, Amanuel Gebisa Aga, Tatek Mamo Wachamo

items.title: Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY): A qualitative study of a co-designed healthy weight and wellbeing intervention in two disadvantaged Scottish communities
items.summary: by Julie Cowie, Rhonda Archibald, Scott Findlay, Danielle Hutcheon, Sinéad Currie, Louise Hay, Elizabeth Cook People who are unable to achieve a healthy lifestyle are at greater risk of type II diabetes, some cancers, heart disease, stroke, mobility problems and poor outcomes from disease. For individuals living in disadvantaged areas, life circumstances such as low income, unemployment, working anti-social hours and limited local services present barriers to the challenge of living healthy lives. Working with two disadvantaged communities in Forth Valley, Scotland, we co-designed and implemented an evidence-informed, incentive-based intervention, Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY), to support citizens with healthy weight and wellbeing.
items.author: Julie Cowie, Rhonda Archibald, Scott Findlay et al.

items.title: Perceived importance, self-rated performance satisfaction, learning stress, and practicum experiences among nursing students: A cross-sectional study with supplementary open-ended responses
items.summary: by Hsiu-Wen Tsai, Shu-Ching Chen This cross-sectional study examined nursing students’ perceived importance and self-rated performance satisfaction regarding fundamental nursing practicum competencies, explored learning-stress scores across academic-achievement categories and psychological-counseling history, and descriptively summarized written practicum experiences. All 730 eligible third-year nursing students were invited; 28 did not participate, 702 returned signed consent forms and questionnaires, and 3 incomplete questionnaires were excluded, leaving 699 participants. Importance–performance analysis (IPA) used sample grand means (importance, 4.679; performance satisfaction, 4.503) as crosshairs. Paired importance–performance gaps and 95% confidence intervals were calculated, and 5,000 bootstrap samples assessed coordinate uncertainty and quadrant stability. Exploratory grade-group and counseling-history comparisons used analysis of variance and independent-samples t tests, respectively, with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction.
items.author: Hsiu-Wen Tsai, Shu-Ching Chen

items.title: Amplified MS2 labeling reveals heterogeneous dynamics of RNA granules in the live murine brain ex vivo
items.summary: by Hyungsik Lim, Grace P. Cooper Dynamics of messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) and the complexes with associated proteins (RNPs), also known as RNA granules, provide post-transcriptional control of gene expression. This regulation is crucial for cell-type diversity and activity-dependent plasticity of the mammalian central nervous system (CNS). However, elucidating the physiological significance of RNA granules has been hampered by technical difficulties to probe them in live brain. Here, we describe a novel method to visualize RNA granules in native CNS tissues of mouse. To amplify the fluorescence signal from single mRNAs incorporating MS2 stem loops, MS2 capsid protein (MCP) was conjugated with 4 tandem superfolder green fluorescent proteins (sfGFPs).
items.author: Hyungsik Lim, Grace P. Cooper

items.title: Antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella and Escherichia coli in fresh vegetables from Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso: Prevalence, β-lactamase genes, and food safety implications
items.summary: by Adama Pamba Séré, Nabèrè Ouattara, Abdoudramane Sanou, Roger Dakuyo, Kabakdé Kaboré, Donatien Kaboré, Kiessoun Konaté, Mamoudou Hama Dicko Fresh vegetables consumed raw are a recognized but underappreciated vehicle for foodborne pathogens and antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria, yet data on AMR determinants in fresh produce remain scarce for West Africa. This cross-sectional study characterized the prevalence of Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp . in 300 fresh vegetable samples from farms, markets, restaurants, and supermarkets in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, along with their antimicrobial resistance profiles, selected β-lactamase genes, and associated food-handling risk factors. E. coli was detected in 63.0% of samples (95% CI: 57.4–68.3%) and Salmonella spp.
items.author: Adama Pamba Séré, Nabèrè Ouattara, Abdoudramane Sanou et al.

items.title: Multi-Probe Cosmological Constraints on Clustering DBI Dark Energy Scenario
items.summary: We present a multi-probe observational analysis of a clustering tachyonic Dirac-Born-Infeld~(DBI) dark energy model. Its noncanonical kinetic term gives a subluminal sound speed, so dark energy perturbations can grow on subhorizon scales. Working in a multifluid framework that tracks both the background expansion and linear perturbations, we constrain the model with nested sampling, using Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, $fσ_8$ growth data, and three Type Ia supernova compilations: Pantheon$+$, DES-SN5YR, and Union3. The standard cosmological parameters agree with $Λ$CDM within $2σ$, with DBI preferring a slightly lower $H_0$ and higher $Ω_{m0}$, with the largest shift being $\simeq1.8σ$ in $H_0$ for Pantheon$+$.
items.author: Samit Ganguly, Surhud More, Goutam Manna et al.

items.title: Players picked on form not club location - Tandy

items.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
items.summary: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|α\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent states (SPACS) generated via coherent seeding possess a quantum relative entropy that precisely quantifies the entanglement deficit between signal and idler fields.
items.author: Tai Hyun Yoon

items.title: Six tournaments, 11 goals - Ronaldo's World Cup legacy
items.summary: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football having scored 146 goals and 234 caps for his country. Here's a look back at his 11 World Cup goals, across six tournaments since 2006.

items.title: Crosstalk-Induced Row Hammer Attacks on Quantum Random Access Codes
items.summary: Quantum processors remain susceptible to crosstalk-induced effects despite the continuous evolution of their underlying hardware architectures. In this work, we experimentally investigate the effectiveness of crosstalk-induced attacks across six IBM superconducting quantum processors and one IQM processor. Our results demonstrate that such attacks can be launched across all the platforms, due to persistance of crosstalk, although their effectiveness varies significantly between devices. The probability of a measurement outcome flip in the victim qubits reaches a maximum value of $60\%$. Also, it is seen that processors sharing identical coupling graphs exhibit different vulnerability profiles, indicating that connectivity alone is insufficient to predict attack efficiency.
items.author: Fernando Almaguer-Angeles, Victor F. dos Santos, Jonas Maziero et al.

items.title: Gloucestershire to rebrand as Bristol for T20 Blast
items.summary: Gloucestershire will compete under the name of Bristol in the T20 Blast from next season in a big to attract new audiences and address falling revenue.

items.title: 400,000-year-old teeth reveal a stunning twist in human evolution
items.summary: A groundbreaking discovery is rewriting the story of human evolution, revealing that an ancient human species once thought to be an evolutionary dead end may have left genetic traces in people alive today.

items.title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
items.summary: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time. This approach enables an experimentally validated, fast (97 ns) and high-fidelity (99.40(9)%) CZ gate, where error analysis reveals that gate errors arise mainly from static decoherence. The scheme facilitates fast, high-quality all-microwave gate operations with a simple topology and can be applied across various quantum platforms.
items.author: Wan-Peng Gao, Xiao-Liang He, Zheng-Qi Niu et al.

items.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
items.summary: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model.
items.author: Oliver O'Brien, Atsushi Ueda, Etienne Granet et al.

items.title: Hubble Learns Galactic History From Stars
items.summary: This Hubble image features the sparkling collection of stars named Messier 30 (M30), also called NGC 7099.

items.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
items.summary: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate.
items.author: Christian Dioguardi

items.title: Scientists discover mysterious “lonely” brain waves linked to memory loss

items.title: Negative non-linear differential dissipation in mechanical quartz resonators
items.summary: We observe negative non-linear differential dissipation in a low-frequency (32.7 kHz) miniature quartz tuning fork, representing a high-Q piezoelectric resonator, at temperatures below 0.3 K. Similar drive-induced dissipation suppression has previously been reported in superconducting microwave resonators, and high-frequency MEMS devices, associated to coupling with tunneling two-level systems (TTLSs). In the case of low-frequency resonators, the equivalent temperature of the mechanical mode is orders of magnitude lower than the thermodynamic temperature of the device, implying that accessible TTLS states are largely saturated. We demonstrate that the observed temperature and drive dependence of the losses fit well within the framework of an interacting TTLS bath, indicating the presence of a channel for energy transfer between the mechanical mode and thermally activated TTLSs.
items.author: Elena Sergeicheva, Juuso Manninen, Juha Tuoriniemi et al.

items.title: Continuous variable payload transmitter for the SPOQC mission
items.summary: The continuous variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) scheme enables two parties to share a secret key separated by a certain distance. Here we propose, design, build, test and show results of a CV payload transmitter, intended to demonstrate downlink based QKD from a CubeSat in low earth orbit. This is part of the SPOQC mission by Quantum Communications Hub, UK which was successfully launched on March 2026.

items.title: Agroforestry ambitions fifty years after launch of a governance-people-science boundary concept.
items.summary: A novel word connecting agriculture and forestry, agroforestry, originated in 1976 with ambitions for radically better land use. At its 50'th anniversary, we reflect on its use in boundary work interfacing governance, people and science. Agroforestry as applied science started with describing the worlds' farmed lands with trees' in their eco-geographical and socio-historical context as plot/farm-level agroforestry ('AF1'). In the 1990's, attention shifted to the landscape scale AF2 and to a policy scale AF3. Simultaneously, climate-tree-soil-crop interactions, bio-economic, and social-ecological systems were further analysed. Searching in the Google Scholar database for 'agroforestry' we selected a 1007 well-cited publications (1979-2025) corpus with a total of 175,081 citations.
items.author: van Noordwijk M, Plieninger T, Rizvi J, Ifejika Speranza C, Dupraz C.

items.title: A modular lentiviral system for multiplexed gene perturbation and functional analysis suggests interdependence of hormone receptors in breast cancer growth in vivo.
items.summary: Precise and flexible control of gene expression is essential for dissecting gene function in complex biological systems. Although recent developments in genetic engineering and CRISPR/Cas9 technology have expanded tools for gene activation, suppression, and editing, their application in physiologically relevant models remains challenging, time-consuming, and expensive. Here, we present a modular, doxycycline-inducible vector system that integrates gene overexpression, shRNA-mediated knockdown, and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated regulation within a single, lentivirus-compatible system. The modular design allows rapid exchange of selection markers, epitope tags, and reporters via Gateway cloning, providing broad adaptability across experimental settings. In addition to standard fluorescent and luminescent reporters, the system includes advanced sensors, such as Fucci cell cycle reporters, to enable monitoring of cellular processes.
items.author: Alam S, Matvienko D, Boström J, Pires MJ, Papadimitropoulou A, Eshtad S, Sanjiv K, Qian H, Valerie NC, Brisken C, Altun M.

items.title: An unsupervised explainable AI reveals oligonucleotide-usage zones matching 2,000 chromosome bands.
items.summary: Unsupervised and explainable AI can uncover genomic features beyond human expectations. Oligonucleotides such as penta- and hexanucleotides often function as core binding motifs for regulatory proteins, and their usage provides powerful tools in functional genomics. We applied an unsupervised, explainable AI to their odds-ratio profiles of all 1-Mb euchromatic fragments in the human genome. Clustering using penta- or hexanucleotide odds ratios (1,024 or 4,096 variables) unexpectedly revealed nearly 2,000 distinct zones. CG-containing penta- and hexanucleotides (244 and 1,185 variables) produced comparable ∼2,000 zones, indicating fundamental genomic segmental structures. Human chromosomes exhibit Giemsa-banding patterns comprising 850 bands at prometaphase and ∼2,000 at prophase.
items.author: Ikemura T, Iwasaki Y, Wada K, Wada Y, Abe T.

items.title: Clinical Heterogeneity in Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1: Identifying Phenotype Categories Using Unsupervised Clustering.
items.summary: Background and objectives Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a genetic multisystem disorder with a wide variability in symptom severity and symptom co-occurrence. This study aimed to identify homogeneous patient subgroups in DM1 with distinct disease characteristics, determine key features underlying these subgroups, and evaluate their potential to inform clinical care and individualized therapy. Methods Adult patients with genetically confirmed DM1 were assessed during annual visits to the Dutch DM1 expert center using standardized examinations and questionnaires to characterize disease burden. K-means cluster analysis was conducted on 10 baseline parameters that reflect the multisystemic disease impact of DM1. External validation was conducted using baseline data from the END-DM1 natural history study.
items.author: la Fontaine LA, de Kok JWTM, Imkamp M, van As D, Bruijnes JE, 't Hoen PAC, Vosse BAH, van Kuijk SMJ, Merkies ISJ, Faber CG, Mul K, Myodraft Consortium and the Myotonic Dystrophy Clinical Research Network.

items.title: Natural History of Limb Girdle Muscular Dystrophy D1 (LGMDD1): A GRASP-LGMD Consortium Study.
items.summary: Background and objectives Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type D1 (LGMDD1) is caused by dominantly inherited pathogenic variants in DNAJB6, a cochaperone of HSP70. Prior work has described the clinical spectrum of LGMDD1, including genotype-phenotype correlations and cross-sectional functional impairments, but prospective longitudinal data remain limited. The primary objective of this study was to identify outcome assessments that reliably measure disease progression in LGMDD1 and are most suitable for use as end points in future natural history and interventional studies. Methods As part of the Genetic Resolution and Assessments Solving Phenotypes in LGMD (GRASP-LGMD) study, participants with genetically confirmed LGMDD1 were enrolled across 11 sites and completed 2 consecutive baseline visits and a 12-month follow-up.
items.author: Findlay AR, Hunn SM, Jones AS, Butler A, Sasidharan S, Hayes M, Statland JM, Strahler T, Will R, Wicklund MP, Dixon SE, Stinson NS, Leung DG, Clause AR, Alfano LN, Weihl C, Johnson NE, as the GRASP-LGMD Consortium.

items.title: Single-episome delivery of BOSMK with miR-142-gated KLF4 streamlines PBMC reprogramming to iPSCs.
items.summary: Peripheral blood-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are attractive for clinical applications, yet multi-plasmid episomal protocols reduce delivery completeness and complicate good manufacturing practice (GMP) workflows. Here, we assembled OCT4, SOX2, MYC, BCL-XL, and KLF4 into a single OriP/EBNA1 episome and tuned KLF4 expression by placing it under the elongation factor 1 alpha (EF1α) promoter with 2 tandem miR-142-3p target sites in its 3'UTR. Across donors, the single-episome system produced robust day-14 colony yields normalized per 1 × 10 5 input cells. A green fluorescent protein (GFP) reporter demonstrated hematopoietic miR-142-dependent suppression, and the miR-gated construct exhibited significantly faster EBNA1 sequence loss by day 4.
items.author: Li X, Wen W, Chang JQ, Zhang F, Gao ZY, Zhang SM, Li GH, Liu B, Wang J, Li H, Cheng CY, Zhang LM, Zhang JP, Zhang XB.

items.title: Real-World Treatment Patterns, Tolerability, and Outcomes Among Patients With CLL/SLL Treated With First-Line Ibrutinib, Acalabrutinib, or Zanubrutinib in the US Community Oncology Setting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.summary: Background Covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (cBTKis) are standard first-line (1L) therapies for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). In clinical trials, second-generation (2G) cBTKis demonstrated better tolerability than ibrutinib, particularly regarding cardiotoxicity; however, real-world evidence on their use, discontinuation, and tolerability remains limited. This study examined treatment patterns and outcomes of cBTKis in the US community oncology setting. Methods CLL/SLL patients who initiated 1L therapy between November 21, 2019 and July 31, 2023 were identified from electronic health records. Kaplan-Meier methods estimated time to treatment discontinuation (TTD), time to next treatment or death (TTNT-D), real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS), and overall survival (OS).
items.author: Burke JM, Zackon I, Wang Y, Aguilar KM, Murphy J, Wayne B, Prescott J, Leng S, Kim I, Chirovsky D, de Nigris E.

items.title: Characteristics and Hospital Outcomes of Patients Admitted to the Intensive Care Unit Because of Haematological Malignancy-A Service Evaluation.
items.summary: Introduction Intensive care unit (ICU) admission due to haematological malignancy (HM) has previously been questioned due to high mortality. While mortality-associated factors have been studied in HM patients to guide decision making and clinical practice, UK-based research remains limited. This single-centre retrospective service evaluation (SE) aimed to review characteristics and hospital outcomes of patients admitted to our ICU because of HM. Methods Consecutive adults with HM-related admissions to a multi-specialty ICU between January 2022 and October 2024 were retrospectively identified. Data were extracted for patient characteristics, ICU interventions and hospital outcomes. Associations with ICU mortality rates were also assessed. Results During the SE, there were 227 ICU admissions of HM patients, of which 168 were HM-related and, hence, included in subsequent analysis.
items.author: Harriman A, Parekh D, Hodson J, Weblin J, MacBean V.

items.title: Closing the loop: a needs-assessment informed model for embedding a non-allergist penicillin allergy de-labelling service in acute medicine, a quality improvement report.
items.summary: Objectives To describe and evaluate a needs-assessment informed model for embedding a non-allergist penicillin allergy de-labelling (PADL) service within an Acute Medical Unit (AMU), including stakeholder experience. Methods A four-phase quality improvement project in one UK AMU, reported per SQUIRE 2.0. Phase 1: needs-assessment survey of 124 staff (pharmacists, doctors, nurses, immunology staff). Phase 2: a multidisciplinary team translated Phase 1 barriers into a PEN-FAST-guided direct oral amoxicillin challenge (DOC) protocol delivered by acute medicine consultants and pharmacists; design decisions were retrospectively mapped to the capability, opportunity and motivation model for behavioural change and Behaviour Change Wheel. Phase 3: DOC in 60 adult inpatients penicillin allergy labels.

items.title: Development of a national outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT) pathway for skin and soft tissue infections in Scotland.
items.summary: Background and objectives The Scottish Antimicrobial Prescribing Group (SAPG) formed a multidisciplinary outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT) working group in September 2020 to develop a national consensus on OPAT treatments and to support service development. Methods The development of a national OPAT skin and soft tissue (SSTI) clinical pathway for adults was identified as a key initiative to support admission avoidance. The pathway was modelled on an established pathway in one health board and agreed by consensus with representation from 12 of the 14 territorial Scottish health boards. A survey to assess pathway uptake was conducted in February 2025, and a follow-up survey of boards that had not adopted the pathway was conducted in April 2026.

items.title: Early terminated transcripts and missing proteins reflect artifacts in bacterial proteomes.
items.summary: The high redundancy of many bacterial proteomes can be used to evaluate proteome quality and identify sequence errors. We have used MMseqs2 clustering with subsequent filtering to identify clusters that contain sequences from at least 50% of the clustered proteomes to build sets of core proteins that include proteins from 95% of the clustered bacteria. These clusters typically capture >80% of proteins in the bacteria. Because these clusters have highly uniform length (the median cluster has >99% of its proteins at the mode length), short ( 133%) proteins are likely artifacts. Most "outlier" proteins are found in fewer than 10% of clusters, and "high-outlier" clusters are over-represented in a small fraction of proteomes, which often have poor proteome BUSCO fragment scores.
items.author: Insana G, Martin MJ, Pearson WR.

items.title: Vibration-Controlled Transient Elastography (VCTE)-Based Prevalence and Assessment of Hepatic Steatosis and Fibrosis in a UK Tertiary Hospital-Based Specialist Weight Management Service: A Real-World Evaluation.
items.summary: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is common in severe obesity; however, liver health assessment is inconsistently implemented in specialist weight management services and real-world data are scarce. This study evaluated the prevalence and severity of vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE)-defined hepatic steatosis and fibrosis risk in adults attending a UK-based Tier 3 specialist weight management service, and explored associations with clinical and metabolic characteristics. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 96 adults referred to a specialist weight management service who underwent baseline VCTE (FibroScan) between June 2024 and November 2025. Controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) estimated hepatic steatosis and fibrosis risk, respectively.
items.author: Willis SA, Ahsan M, Rathi K, Lawrence I, Davies MJ, Webb DR, King JA, Ahmad E.

items.title: Comparison of Effects of Pulsed Field Ablation and Cryoablation on Left Atrial Stiffness Using Invasively Derived Pressure-Volume Relationship.
items.summary: Background Acute effects of pulsed field ablation (PFA) on passive atrial mechanical properties have not hitherto been assessed by reconstruction of pressure-volume relationship using invasive intracavitary pressure measurements. Methods In a cohort of 38 first-time atrial fibrillation ablation patients, submitted to pulmonary vein isolation, we studied the effects of PFA and cryoballoon ablation on the left atrial elastic constant and passive elastic chamber stiffness constant, expressing baseline left atrial conditions and quantifying passive left atrial stiffness, respectively. Left atrial pressure was invasively measured immediately pre- and post-procedurally, while volume values were obtained echocardiographically. Results No differences were noted in passive elastic chamber stiffness constant values, pre- and post-procedurally in either group.
items.author: Antoniou CK, Tsiachris D, Karanikola AE, Botis M, Kordalis A, Doundoulakis I, Xydis P, Klettas D, Chrysohoou C, Tsioufis KP.

items.title: Activity of aztreonam-avibactam and comparators against difficult-to-treat resistant Enterobacterales from United States medical centres (2020-24) † .
items.summary: Background The occurrence of infections caused by Gram-negative bacteria with difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR) is rapidly increasing, generally requiring the use of recently approved, last-resort antimicrobial agents or old compounds that are more toxic and/or less effective. We evaluated the activity of aztreonam-avibactam and comparators against DTR Enterobacterales. Methods A total of 42 295 Enterobacterales isolates were consecutively collected (one per patient) from 85 US medical centres in 2020-24 and susceptibility tested by Clinical Laboratory Standards Institute broth microdilution. The collection included 450 carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) and 284 DTR isolates, which were screened for β-lactamases by whole genome sequencing. Results Aztreonam-avibactam was active against 98.2% of DTR (minimum inhibitory concentration for 50%/90% of the collection, 0.25/1 mg/L) and 97.1% of CRE isolates and retained potent activity (≥90.0% susceptibility) against DTR isolates non-susceptible to ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam and/or cefiderocol.
items.author: Sader HS, Kimbrough JH, Debabov D, Papp-Wallace KM, Castanheira M.

items.title: Intraventricular Tuberculoma of the Central Nervous System: A Systematic Review of Clinical Presentation, Management, and Outcome.
items.summary: Background and objectives Tuberculosis remains a major global health burden, with central nervous system (CNS) involvement accounting for 1% to 10% of cases. Intraventricular tuberculoma is a distinct, poorly documented entity, separate from tuberculous meningitis with hydrocephalus. This systematic review assessed the epidemiology, diagnosis, management, and outcomes of CNS intraventricular tuberculoma. Methods PubMed and Scopus were searched per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines for studies on CNS intraventricular tuberculoma (PROSPERO registration number CRD420251017978). Pooled data were summarized using measures of central tendency and dispersion. Results Of 841 records identified, 18 studies (17 case reports, 1 retrospective series) encompassing 30 patients were included.
items.author: Gbenou FBB, Hugues Dokponou YC, Lawson DL, Agada NK, Badirou OBA, Diaby R, Bankole NDA.

items.title: Symptomatic Vertebral Artery Loop Formations: A Scoping Review of Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Treatment.
items.summary: Background and objectives Vertebral artery loop formations (VALFs) are under-reported yet treatable causes of cervical radiculopathy. Incidence varies between 2% and 7.5%. Exact pathogenesis is unclear. Literature is sparse, and optimal treatment remains controversial. This review aims to collect all available literature describing symptomatic VALFs. Methods We performed a scoping review in PubMed, Ovid Medline, Cochrane Library, British Medical Journal, and Google Scholar. Full-text original, descriptive, and analytical studies were collated. Data from retrieved articles were collaboratively reviewed, tabulated, and synthesized. Clinical features, diagnosis, and treatment outcomes were discussed. Results A total of 31 articles and 33 patients found to have symptomatic VALFs were included.
items.author: Tiangco DAL, Sih IMY.

items.title: Manual Brachial Artery Compression as an Adjunct for Intraoperative Hemostasis During Carpal Tunnel Release.
items.summary: Background and objectives Carpal tunnel release (CTR) is typically a straightforward procedure, and major bleeding is uncommon. However, minor oozing may occasionally interfere with visualization during critical steps. We describe a simple adjunctive maneuver using manual brachial artery compression for temporary control of arterial inflow during CTR. Methods This retrospective study describes a consecutive series of 55 patients who underwent CTR under local anesthesia with epinephrine. Manual compression of the brachial artery was applied intermittently to modulate arterial inflow during critical surgical steps. Operative findings and postoperative complications were evaluated. Intraoperative discomfort was retrospectively assessed from nursing records. In a subset of 26 cases with operative video recordings, compression duration and intraoperative bleeding control were evaluated using video review and a 5-point Likert scale by 2 surgical team members.
items.author: Yazaki S, Sato M, Uchida M, Takasuna H, Matsumori T, Kushiro Y, Hidaka G, Tanaka T, Fukuyama R, Tenjin K, Murata H.

items.title: Hybrid Occipital Artery-AICA Bypass Followed by Endovascular Embolization for a Radiation-Induced Dissecting AICA Aneurysm in a Pediatric Patient.
items.summary: Background and importance Pediatric anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) aneurysms are rare; radiation-associated dissecting lesions require exclusion without compromising brainstem or cerebellar perforators. Clinical presentation A 13-year-old boy developed a progressively enlarging right AICA a2 dissecting aneurysm after cranial irradiation for pineal nongerminomatous germ cell tumor. Because direct clipping or isolated parent vessel occlusion was considered high risk, he underwent occipital artery-AICA a3 bypass followed by endovascular coil embolization in a single hybrid session. Dual arterial access enabled transradial vertebral artery treatment and transfemoral angiographic bypass assessment. Postoperative MRI showed a small transient cerebellar ischemic lesion that resolved within 2 weeks.
items.author: Wang X, Liu P, Shalibashvili R, Chai M, Tian Y, Li Z, Shi Y, Song K, Qiu T, Zhu W.

items.title: Hemorrhagic Vulnerability of Lenticulostriate Artery-Supplied Arteriovenous Malformations After Radiosurgery: De Novo Aneurysm Formation on Distal Feeders.
items.summary: Background and objectives Deep arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) carry a substantial risk of hemorrhage during the latency period after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS). We hypothesized that arterial supply involving the lenticulostriate arteries (LSAs), which are representative fragile perforating arteries, contributes to this vulnerability. This study investigated the hemorrhagic propensity and angiographic changes in LSA-supplied AVMs. Methods In this retrospective case series, we identified 13 patients with LSA-supplied AVMs from a database of 140 patients who underwent GKRS between 2010 and 2026. We calculated the annualized hemorrhage rate during the latency period and evaluated emergency angiographic findings to determine precise bleeding sources.
items.author: Sugihara M, Kondoh T, Fujita A, Mizowaki T, Yamamoto Y, Tachizawa N, Kajimoto H, Tanaka H, Takaishi Y, Kohta M, Sasayama T.

items.title: Delayed High-Output Chylothorax Following Thymectomy for Thymoma.
items.summary: Chylothorax is an uncommon complication following thymectomy and results from disruption of the thoracic duct or its tributaries during surgery. We report the case of a 50-year-old man with autoimmune myasthenia gravis who developed a delayed postoperative chylothorax following video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) thymectomy for a type B2 thymoma, Masaoka stage I. On postoperative day 21, the patient presented with acute respiratory distress and severe hypoxemia. Chest computed tomography revealed a large left-sided pleural effusion with extensive passive lung collapse. Thoracentesis in the emergency department evacuated 1.5 L of milky pleural fluid, followed by an additional 4 L after chest tube drainage in the intensive care unit.
items.author: Nafaa M, Bencherki R, Ziati J, Noussair M, Lahcen B.

items.title: Recurrent Unexplained Fever and Suspected Promazine Toxicity: Why Probable Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome Was Left Undiagnosed in a Healthcare Worker.
items.summary: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is a potentially fatal adverse reaction to dopamine-antagonist medication that can resemble sepsis. A 51-year-old woman working in healthcare experienced recurrent episodes of fever, confusion and muscle rigidity, with six hospital presentations over approximately 10 months. Her prescribed medicines included promazine and amitriptyline. During an earlier severe admission, she developed hyperthermia, agitation, shock, and a creatine kinase concentration of 7272 U/L, requiring intensive care. Investigations did not identify a unifying diagnosis. During the most recent admission, review of previous records and a non-judgemental discussion elicited possible use of additional medication for sleep and neuropathic pain, although the preparation and quantity remained unclear.
items.author: Makstutis S, Collins S.

items.title: Molecular Profiling in Asia: The Current Status and Approach.
items.summary: Precision oncology has transformed cancer care globally through biomarker-driven and genomically guided treatment strategies. In Asia, where nearly 60% of the world's population resides, the implementation of molecular profiling presents both significant opportunities and unique challenges. Despite increasing adoption, precision diagnostics remain largely concentrated in urban and academic centers, with disparities in access, infrastructure, and expertise across the region. Advances in next-generation sequencing (NGS), including targeted gene panels, comprehensive genomic profiling, whole exome sequencing, and whole-genome sequencing, have enabled the identification of actionable alterations across multiple tumor types. Liquid biopsy approaches, including circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and circulating tumor cells (CTCs), are further transforming cancer care by enabling real-time disease monitoring and detection of resistance mechanisms.
items.author: Limaye S, Loong H, Bhatt M, Chan KH.

items.title: State of Precision Oncology: An Australian Perspective.
items.summary: Precision oncology is redefining cancer therapeutics worldwide. In Australia, the integration of genomic medicine into routine clinical oncology remains inconsistently constrained by fragmented funding mechanisms, regional disparities, and a limited workforce. Understanding these structural and policy challenges is crucial for transitioning toward a sustainable, equitable genomic health ecosystem. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from national policy frameworks, peer-reviewed literature, and translational oncology initiatives to examine the current state of precision oncology in Australia. Key domains of analysis include clinical practice patterns, access and equity, infrastructure, data governance, regulatory oversight, and health-policy reform. Although major initiatives, such as Omico's Precision Oncology Screening Platform Enabling Clinical Trials (PrOSPeCT) platform, the ZERO Childhood Cancer Program, and the forthcoming national coordination body Genomics Australia, demonstrate substantial progress, significant implementation barriers persist.
items.author: Liaqat S, Khattak MA.

items.title: When the Average is Not Enough: Applying Shewhart Charts with a Sloping Centerline in Healthcare Quality Monitoring.
items.author: Gurmessa OH, Berkessa OL, Bekele BT, Awol IH, Dilo ZS, Workneh WM, Simeneh GT, Wotango BY.

items.title: Molecular Profiling and Precision Oncology for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer in Latin America: Unique Epidemiology, Persistent Barriers, and Paths Toward Equity.
items.summary: Abstract Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) represents a critical public health crisis in Latin America (LA), the leading cause of cancer-associated mortality across the region. Although global incidence rates are shifting, the burden in low- and middle-income countries is projected to increase significantly by 2030. Beyond the impact of tobacco, LA faces unique challenges derived from environmental exposures and diverse genetic ancestry that shape a molecular landscape distinct from other regions. This has resulted in a high prevalence of actionable drivers, particularly EGFR mutations, positioning a large segment of the population as ideal candidates for precision medicine approaches. However, current efforts to address this epidemic fall short of regional needs, as the potential of precision oncology remains largely unrealized due to multilevel systemic and economic barriers.
items.author: Picón CR, Borea R, Rizzo MM, Minatta JN, Amorin RI, Pandolfi JB, Cardona AF, Arrieta O, Enrico D, Voza A, Denninghoff V, Rolfo C.

items.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11336-3 Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
items.author: Paolo Di Achille, Lawrence Cai, Jiang Wu et al.

items.title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11351-4 Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
items.author: Xinyu Chen, Xinyang Guo, Xi Yang et al.

items.title: The surprising reason women in academia do more parenting than men
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03568-0 Policies designed to keep women in the workforce could be entrenching gendered parenting roles.
items.author: Rachel Fieldhouse

items.title: Daily briefing: Toothbrush zaps bacteria to clear plaque
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03596-w The manual toothbrush cleans by generating a bacteria-killing electrical charge. Plus, what ‘historic’ US mid-term results mean for science and a genetics lab run by AI-powered robots.
items.author: Jacob Smith

items.title: Identifying and targeting the Mg-Fe-PmrAB regulatory circuit reverses phosphate starvation-driven polymyxin tolerance in Enterobacteriaceae
items.summary: Phosphate (Pi) scarcity, a pervasive stressor prevalent in bacterial infections and dysbiotic host environments, potently alters antimicrobial susceptibility against cationic antibiotics like polymyxins across diverse bacterial taxa. While established Pi depletion-induced antimicrobial tolerance mechanisms often involve membrane phospholipid remodelling, Enterobacteriaceae largely lack these pathways, leaving the mechanism underlying their adaptation to Pi scarcity unresolved. Here, we reveal that Pi limitation robustly induces polymyxin tolerance in Enterobacteriaceae through 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose (L-Ara4N) modification of the Gram-negative outer membrane component lipid A, reflecting a distinct adaptive strategy. This modification is driven by strong arn operon induction, mediated by the PmrAB two-component system. We discover that Pi depletion triggers cellular Mg2+ release, prompting compensatory Fe3+ mobilization to the cell envelope that directly activates PmrAB.
items.author: ZHANG, G., Deng, Z., JIANG, J. et al.

items.title: Environmental DNA reveals biotic homogenization alongside elevated native and non-native species richness in marinas, supporting an ecological portuarization syndrome
items.summary: The global expansion of ports has created novel marine urban ecosystems that remain understudied. Recent evidence suggests that ports promote distinct evolutionary trajectories due to their unique environmental conditions and the continuous introduction of non-indigenous species (NIS), a phenomenon previously coined the `biological portuarization syndrome`. In this study, we examine the ecological dimension of this concept by using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, to compare animal assemblages in 12 recreational ports (i.e., marinas) with those found in adjacent natural habitats in the north-western Mediterranean Sea. By combining three markers, we identified 536 species belonging to 18 phyla, including 50 species classified as non-indigenous or cryptogenic based on previous records from traditional surveys.
items.author: Lilli, G., Caillarec-Joly, A., Violet, C. et al.

items.title: Scalable methylome-transcriptome profiling resolves clonal organization in human hematopoiesis
items.summary: Understanding human tissue maintenance and remodeling requires linking clonal ancestry to molecular state, yet scalable joint measurement remains challenging. Here, we introduce Droplet-MT and an integrated computational workflow for joint transcriptome and methylome profiling at ~10,000 cells per library. Methylation epimutations enable mutation-independent clonal reconstruction from high-coverage methylomes, while reference-based label transfer assigns cells to established clones at ~0.2% CpG coverage, reducing sequencing cost. Clone-aggregated somatic variants provide genetic annotation without additional single-cell genotyping. Across ~21,000 paired profiles from healthy blood and longitudinal acute myeloid leukemia, we resolved small and expanded clones with heterogeneous lineage output. In leukemia, the framework distinguished changes in malignant clonal abundance, state remodeling within persistent clones, and recovery of healthy polyclonal hematopoiesis.
items.author: Shao, J., Chen, M., Liu, Y. et al.

items.title: Kinship, acoustic signaling, and socio-spatial structure shape shared decisions and social influence in white-nosed coatis
items.summary: When individual preferences for collective outcomes diverge, cohesive animal groups often coalesce on the majority opinion. However, majority-based decision rules may be counterbalanced by other factors, particularly in heterogeneous groups with differentiated social relationships, and these factors could produce inequality in social influence. We used multi-sensor tracking collars to collect detailed and simultaneous data on the movements and vocalizations of almost all members of three wild white-nosed coati (Nasua narica) groups, and analyzed 2,401 individual decisions between conflicting travel directions that were indicated by acoustically signaling groupmates. Decision-making was shared: individuals favored directions that had majority support, and we found evidence that they used acoustic signals and movement cues to infer majority support.
items.author: Winans, J. C., Grout, E. M., Ortega, J. et al.

items.title: Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics reveals selective organization of α-synuclein inclusions
items.summary: -Synuclein inclusions, the lesions typical of Parkinson's disease, have been interpreted as protective deposits, toxic species or failed degradation products, each predicting a different composition and correlating that enrichment with neuron dysfunction and eventual degeneration. Distinguishing them requires measuring what an inclusion concentrates relative to the cell that built it. Here we developed Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics, which uses ultrasensitive mass spectrometry to profile laser-microdissected inclusions against the remainder of the same cell or a matched host. In HEK293 cells, iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons and post-mortem patient brain, each inclusion concentrated a selective subset of its cell's proteome, independent of abundance and dominated by membrane, in neurons largely presynaptic.
items.author: Oeller, M., Vasconez Grunauer, S., Sitron, C. S. et al.

items.title: Clinical-Anchored Incremental Survival Learning: A Stability-Constrained Framework for Molecularly Enhanced Survival Prediction in Lung Adenocarcinoma
items.summary: Accurate survival prediction in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains challenging because high-dimensional molecular data can introduce overfitting and unstable feature selection. We developed Clinical-Anchored Incremental Survival Learning (CAISL), a framework that integrates a sparse molecular risk correction with a clinical baseline to improve prognostic discrimination while constraining model complexity and prediction variability. CAISL was evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas LUAD cohort comprising 470 patients and 119 observed deaths. Performance was compared with clinical Cox, molecular-only, and unanchored multimodal models using five independently seeded, event-stratified five-fold cross-validation runs. CAISL achieved a mean concordance index (C-index) of 0.7246, compared with 0.6970 for clinical Cox, yielding an absolute improvement of 0.0276 (95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI], 0.005 to 0.050).
items.author: Shringarpure, P., Divakar, S., Khobragade, S.

items.title: Amide I kurtosis maps cardiac amyloid in human tissue by ultrabroadband multiplex coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) microscopy
items.summary: Cardiac amyloidosis is caused by deposits of misfolded proteins in the heart and can lead to heart failure. Histological confirmation typically involves staining tissue sections with Congo red and examining them under polarized light for apple-green birefringence; however, achieving an interpretable, label-free, and observer-independent assessment remains challenging. Here we show that Pearson kurtosis of channel intensities within the amide I window provides an interpretable, fitting-free contrast for cardiac amyloid in unstained human cardiac tissue sections imaged by ultrabroadband multiplex coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS). In two participants, high-kurtosis regions corresponded with Congo red-positive tissue in adjacent stained sections (descriptive spatial AUCs, 0.79 and 0.73).
items.author: Ota, K., Chen, T.-H., Yamaguchi, T. et al.

items.title: Genomic prediction of resistance to Phytophthora megakarya in cacao from a sparse host-pathogen screen
items.summary: Black pod rot caused by Phytophthora megakarya is a major disease impacting cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) production in West Africa. Resistance is influenced by genetic variation in both host and pathogen populations. While genomic prediction approaches have been widely applied in plant breeding, most studies incorporate only host genomic information. The value of explicitly modeling pathogen genomic relatedness in quantitative disease prediction remains largely unknown. We genotyped 947 clones from the International Cacao Collection at CATIE using a 10K-SNP panel and characterized 67 P. megakarya isolates by sequencing 3,505 virulence-associated genes and 2,774 SNP loci. Cacao clones were extensively admixed, while isolates formed three geographically structured subpopulations.
items.author: Schlathoelter, I., Gitto, A. J., Arciniegas, A. L. et al.

items.title: Gene regulatory architecture in antibiotic resistance is optimized for specific dynamic regimens
items.summary: Cellular responses to antibiotics face a fundamental trade-off: resistance must be deployed quickly enough to prevent the accumulation of drug inside the cell, but expression of resistance genes is costly in the absence of the drug. Therefore, antibiotic responses are typically regulated, controlling not only whether resistance is expressed, but also when, how strongly, and for how long. These regulatory strategies are implemented through the strength and arrangement of promoters and operators. However, it is still not clear how the dynamics of drug exposure select for specific regulatory strategies. Here, we develop a dynamical model of a typical antibiotic response, where a transcriptional repressor senses the drug and regulates expression of a resistance protein, coupled to the effects of the drug on cell growth and gene expression.
items.author: Geng, H., Schultz, D.

items.title: Identification of T-Cell specific signature miRNAs and target pathways in Psoriasis
items.summary: Psoriasis is a chronic skin disease characterized by keratinocyte hyperproliferation, involving T cells as the major players in the manifestation of lesional and systemic inflammation. With the extensive exploration of keratinocyte dysfunctionality, T cell centric deregulation has gained much focus with limited molecular understanding in the context of disease etiology. miRNAs, the molecular switches known to drive disease manifestation via altering keratinocyte biology, have not been much studied in the context of T cell alterations. This study aims to explore T cell-associated miRNAs and their target signaling networks to understand their role in modulating psoriasis specific T cell changes. miRNAs with altered expression in psoriatic T cells were identified through a comprehensive analysis of the available literature and datasets.
items.author: Madaan, P., Tyagi, N., Tyagi, S. et al.

items.title: Dissociating Resting-State Networks of Pedohebephilic Preference and Child Sexual Offending Using Network-Based Prediction
items.summary: Pedohebephilia (P+), the sexual preference for prepubescent and early pubertal minors, regularly causes distress in those affected. While associated with child sexual offending (CSO), P+ is not a prerequisite for CSO. Limited neuroimaging studies have identified alterations associated with P+, while these may primarily reflect offending history. The correlates of P+ independent of CSO therefore remain unclear. We examined this distinction using intrinsic functional networks within a multivariate predictive framework. Using resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) and network-based prediction (NBS-Predict), we performed pairwise classifications among non-offending pedohebephilic men (P+CSO-, n=35), pedohebephilic men with CSO (P+CSO+, n=38), and non-pedohebephilic controls without CSO (P-CSO-, n=63).
items.author: Serin, E., Khan, K. R., Krueger, T. et al.

items.title: Sex differences in cell type-specific transcriptional programs and GPCR signaling in the human subgenual anterior cingulate cortex
items.summary: Psychiatric conditions show marked sex differences in disease onset, symptom presentation, and response to treatments. Understanding how sex differences manifest across molecularly distinct neuronal populations in individuals without psychiatric conditions may help explain sex-dependent variation in neural circuit function and treatment response. Here, we examined molecularly distinct cell types within the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) of non-psychiatric subjects. Using RNA sequencing data previously generated from laser-capture microdissected neurons, we investigated sex differences in gene expression and co-expression networks in excitatory pyramidal neurons (layers 2/3 and 5/6) and somatostatin (SST)-, parvalbumin (PVALB)-, and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-expressing inhibitory interneurons (N=10 males, 9 females).
items.author: Snowden, A. W., Li, N. Y., Sibille, E. et al.

items.title: Temporal stability for individual differences in both habit learning and expression
items.summary: Actions transition from goal-directed to stimulus-driven habits through repetition. Individual differences in the capacity to learn and control habits are central to current models of psychopathology, which assume that overreliance on habitual control drives maladaptive behaviors. However, whether these tendencies reflect stable, trait-like cognitive processes remains unclear. We examined the temporal stability of individual differences in habit learning and expression. Across two preregistered experiments (total N = 313), we assessed stimulus-response habits using the same stimuli after one day or different stimuli after four months. Evidence for stable individual differences in habit commissions was strong and comparable across experiments, with computational modelling further supporting trait-like tendencies for habit learning and expression.
items.author: Martinez-Lopez, P., Leon, J. J., Garre-Frutos, F. et al.

items.title: The C. elegans Connectome Toolbox: an open, extensible framework for multimodal connectomic data integration and analysis
items.summary: The nematode C. elegans is one of the best studied model organisms in biology. Since the initial description of the C. elegans neuronal connectome by White and colleagues, numerous studies have mapped and analyzed the connectome, and released structured datasets of the connectivity, often merging and adding to previous versions. These datasets now serve as foundational resources that underpin studies into the neuronal basis of C. elegans behavior. In spite of their high utility, heterogeneity in the different datasets and their annotation conventions obscures direct comparison where discrepancies between connectomes frequently stem from differences in coverage or nomenclature rather than genuine biological disagreement.
items.author: Vickneswaran, Y., Ponzi, A., Sinha, A. et al.

items.title: 40 Hz visual stimulation increases gamma-band functional connectivity between visual, parietal and frontal regions
items.summary: Visual stimulation at 40 Hz is being investigated as a non-invasive intervention for Alzheimer's disease. Its neural responses have been reported in regions beyond the visual cortex, and concurrent cognitive tasks have been shown to increase their spatial extent. However, it is unclear whether these responses reflect increased functional connectivity between regions or a common response to the stimulus, and whether a concurrent task changes this connectivity. We recorded EEG from 29 healthy young adults during Regular 40 Hz flicker and Irregular 30-50 Hz flicker, each with and without a target-counting task (2 x 2 within-participant design). Source-space connectivity between visual, parietal, and frontal regions was estimated with the debiased squared weighted phase-lag index (dWPLI).
items.author: Ma, T., Sun, Q., Mlinaric, T. et al.

items.title: Social vision expands into auditory cortices of people born deaf: evidence from naturalistic film and encoding models
items.summary: Comparing deaf and hearing adults provides insight into the contribution of experience to function of auditory cortical networks. We used naturalistic fMRI and voxel-wise encoding to measure information processing in auditory networks of deaf (n=24) and hearing (n=22) adults who watched a 35-minute silent animated film. Unlike simpler stimuli, naturalistic films are rich in a broad range of perceptual, affective, and social features, including motion, dynamic social interactions, and Theory of Mind. Machine vision algorithms and human coding were used to densely annotate visual and social film features. In both groups we observed a right-lateralized processing hierarchy with encoding of low-level visual features in early visual areas, social visual features along the superior temporal sulcus (STS) and Theory of Mind in temporoparietal junction.
items.author: Zimmermann, M., Szwed, M., Isik, L. et al.

items.title: Increased activity without changes in coupling between somata and apical dendrites during visual mismatches
items.summary: Leading theories of cortical function posit that sensory processing involves a comparison between top-down predictions and bottom-up sensory data. Tests of these theories have been hampered by experimental challenges related to simultaneously recording top-down and bottom-up signals in response to sensory stimuli that either do or do not match internally-generated predictions. Here, we conduct dual-plane 2-photon calcium imaging near-simultaneously from distal apical dendrites and somata of pyramidal neurons in each of 4 different regions of mouse visual cortex while the mice are presented with visual sequences that can either match or mismatch previously habituated visual stimuli. Specifically, we examine the responses in the distal apical dendrites and cell bodies of pyramidal neurons while mice view either movie clips that reverse unexpectedly or Gabor patch sequences that have orientations that do not match habituated patterns.
items.author: Henley, T. M., Tindall, J., Pina, J. E. et al.

items.title: Clonally Convergent Tph/Tfh-like CD4+ T Cells are Shared Across Recovery and Recurrence in Experimental Periodontitis
items.summary: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the tooth-supporting structures (periodontium) that requires life-long maintenance to prevent progression. Using a sensitized model of recurrent periodontitis in mice (SeRPD), in which regulatory breakdown was induced by temporary Treg depletion concurrent with disease, we mapped the gingival T cell imprint across each disease phase. Transient regulatory breakdown left a durable mucosal imprint after clinical recovery, characterized by enrichment of local and regional CD4 T cells. Paired single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing of gingival immune cells identified a convergent clonotype expanded from recovery into recurrence that carried a Tfh/Tph-like transcriptional identity. An analogous CD4 T cell population was detected in human periodontitis lesions by single-cell transcriptomics.
items.author: Sharma, A., Olmedo, V., Rojas, L. et al.

items.title: Temperature alters Culex tarsalis West Nile virus vector competence, tissue bottlenecks, and transcriptional responses
items.summary: West Nile virus is an arbovirus transmitted by Culex mosquitoes. Temperature is frequently the strongest abiotic factor impacting transmission in many virus-vector pairings, including WNV and Culex. However, it is unknown how temperature impacts WNV population bottlenecks and transcriptional responses to infection in Culex tarsalis. We found that elevated temperatures led to increased likelihood of transmission of rare virus variants due to increased vector competence and less stringent tissue barriers. Analysis of Cx. tarsalis transcriptional responses confirmed that WNV infection had minimal impacts on transcriptional activity. Temperature, however, induced significant changes to mosquito gene expression, whereas canonical immune gene expression minimally changed in response to infection.
items.author: Gallichotte, E. N., King, D. C., Marsico, B. et al.

items.title: RNA Polymerase Backtracking Promotes Type III-A CRISPR DNA Targeting
items.summary: Type III CRISPR-Cas systems provide transcription-dependent immunity against mobile genetic elements, yet the mechanism underlying their DNA targeting remains unclear. Although the type III effector Cas10-Csm functions as a single-stranded DNase in vitro, type III systems eliminate double-stranded DNA targets in vivo, suggesting that transcription generates critical DNA substrates. Here, we show that conserved RNA polymerase anti-backtracking factors, such as GreA, selectively inhibit DNA-targeting of type III immunity. GreA overexpression abolishes protection against both phages and conjugative plasmids, whereas mutations that disrupt GreA anti-backtracking activity eliminate this effect. In contrast, immunity mediated by the type II CRISPR-Cas system or the auxiliary type III RNase Csm6 remain unaffected, demonstrating that GreA specifically suppresses Cas10-dependent DNA interference.
items.author: Hernandez Viera, A. J., Gross, N. R., Tran, P. Q. et al.

items.title: Phage lysates are reservoirs of biologically active quorum sensing signals
items.summary: Bacteriophage lysates are widely used to study phage-bacterial interactions and are typically applied after filtration without further purification. As a result, host-derived metabolites produced during phage propagation are transferred alongside phage particles, yet the biological consequences of this carryover remain largely unexplored. Here, we show that the Pseudomonas aeruginosa quorum sensing signal PQS persists in a bioactive state in phage lysates for at least one year. In contrast, the quorum sensing molecules 3OC12-HSL and C4-HSL are rapidly degraded. We demonstrate that PQS stability is caused by its association with outer membrane vesicles, which protect the signal from degradation. PQS from phage lysates induces production of the virulence factor pyocyanin and increases mortality in a Galleria mellonella model of P.
items.author: Eichler, A. H., Mauritzen, J. J., Koonce, K. C. et al.

items.title: Pneumocystis phosphoglucomutase links glucose-phosphate metabolism to β-1,3-glucan synthesis and cell-wall integrity
items.summary: The fungal cell wall is a dynamic, carbohydrate-rich structure whose composition is closely coordinated with cellular metabolism. Phosphoglucomutase (PGM) interconverts glucose-1-phosphate and glucose-6-phosphate, linking carbon metabolism with UDP-glucose-dependent cell-wall biosynthesis. We previously identified functional Pgm2 homologs from Pneumocystis jirovecii and Pneumocystis murina. Here, using a Saccharomyces cerevisiae pgm2{Delta} complementation model, we examined the relationship between Pgm2 activity, {beta}-1,3-glucan, and cell-wall integrity. Pgm2 deficiency reduced {beta}-1,3-glucan content and altered zymolyase sensitivity without major changes in cell-wall thickness. Bulk RNA sequencing revealed that the pgm2{Delta} mutant exhibited coordinated metabolic and cell-wall transcriptional responses, including increased SLT2/MPK1, RLM1, FKS2/GSC2, GFA1, CHS1, CRH1, SED1, and CWP1 expression and decreased FKS1, GAS1, GAS3, and CHS2 expression.
items.author: Kottom, T., McLean, J. L., Limper, A. H.

items.title: Optimal compositions of potent sliced-siRNA with DNA bases substitution and insights of Ago2 slicing actions
items.summary: We have previously characterized the nucleotide compositions of single-stranded ago2-sliced small interfering RNAs (sliced-siRNA, sliRNA), a novel type of potent RNAi trigger designed based on the biogenesis mechanism of miRNA-451. sliRNAs have on par antisense mediated silencing activity but about 1000-fold reduced passenger strand activity compared to siRNA. In the current study, to further characterize sliRNAs to facilitate their in vivo application, we have investigated the effects of substituting RNA nucleotides (nts) in sliRNA with DNA nts (sliDRNAs), which will allow us to study the potential effects on their processing, maturation, and silencing activity from individual or multiple nts at different positions.
items.author: Sun, G., Lizhar, E. M., Shi, Y. et al.

items.title: Insulin stimulation induces dynamic interaction between 14-3-3 and the C-terminal tail domain of Kinesin-2 subunit KIF3B in vitro
items.summary: Heterotrimeric kinesin[ndash]2 mediates diverse intracellular transport processes, yet the mechanisms governing its cargo specificity and regulation remain poorly understood. In this study, we report the regulation of interaction between the kinesin[ndash]2 subunit KIF3B and a candidate adaptor protein, 14[ndash]3[ndash]3[epsilon];. Using splitAPEX2 proximity labelling and fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) assays in HEK293T cells, we demonstrate that 14[ndash]3[ndash]3[epsilon]; interacts with KIF3B within discrete subcellular compartments. This interaction is significantly enhanced upon insulin stimulation, indicating regulation by signalling pathways. Time resolved FLIM analysis further reveals that the site of interaction is dynamic, suggesting spatial and temporal control of motora[ndash]daptor association. Finally, the interactions are mapped to two serine residues in the C[ndash]terminal tail region of KIF3B that are highly conserved across species.

items.title: N-terminal cysteine independent effects of oxidative stress on the stability of RGS4 and 5
items.summary: Oxidative post-translational modifications on the sulfhydryl group of cysteines can occur spontaneously or enzymatically. The enzymatic dioxygenation of N-terminal cysteines has emerged as a new oxygen sensing paradigm, catalysed by 2-aminoethanethiol dioxygenase (ADO) in mammals. Conflicting evidence has been reported in recent years on whether this reaction can occur spontaneously in the absence of ADO. Here we sought to address whether cellular oxidative stress can interfere with ADO-catalysed N-terminal cysteine dioxygenation. Using a system to produce titratable intracellular levels of H2O2, we demonstrate that the stability of RGS4 and 5 is not affected by physiological levels of oxidative stress, whether ADO is present or not.

items.title: Variation in the embryonic cell lineages of Caenorhabditis elegans natural populations
items.summary: Developmental variation has often been appreciated as a major phenotypic substrate of evolutionary innovation in multicellular organisms. Although quantification of developmental variation in isogenic populations has a long history, it has been difficult to accomplish across natural populations until recently. Given its invariant cell lineage, Caenorhabditis elegans represents an ideal model system for studying how natural diversity in development is expressed at the resolution of single cells, cell lineages, and the whole embryo. Using embGAN, a deep-learning pipeline that enables label-free lineage tracing without the bottleneck and potential confounding effects of generating transgenic strains, we reconstructed the early embryonic lineage of 78 embryos spanning eight genetic backgrounds, including six wild strains, and quantified cell-cycle timing with a lineage-aligned graph metric that separates global rescaling of developmental rate from localized changes in lineage structure.
items.author: Weymer, C., Johnson, R. L., Helou, J. O. et al.

items.title: Phenotypic Plasticity in Sub-Antarctic Plants: Costs, Environmental Complexity, and the Facilitative Role of Trait Integration
items.summary: Phenotypic plasticity is one plant response to climate warming, but it may incur costs and be either limited or facilitated by trait integration or simultaneous environmental shifts such as shading. Empirical studies addressing these costs and limitations across populations or maternal lineages, and how they vary with environmental context, remain scarce. We studied three plant species from the sub-Antarctic Kerguelen Islands, a region undergoing rapid warming, growing seeds from multiple source populations under different temperature and light treatments. We measured plasticity, performance, and morphological integration in young plants. Plants from more plastic source populations performed worse, while those from more integrated populations were more plastic, consistent with the facilitation hypothesis.
items.author: Hennion, F., Labarrere, B., Renaudon, M. et al.

items.title: A timeline for evolution of metabolism in early microbes
items.summary: The metabolism of early microbes shaped our planet's chemistry and enabled more life to evolve. However, it remains uncertain when many forms of metabolism arose and which organisms carried them out. Here we combine machine learning, metabolic networks, and phylogenomics of microbes to date 14 forms of metabolism and 6 other traits. We find that metabolism evolved in three waves, starting >3.4 billion years ago (Ga) with fermentation and sulfur compound respiration. A second wave began ~3.2 Ga with aerobic respiration and growth, while a third began ~1.4 Ga with further specialization. We compared these predictions with independent dates from the geochemical record, and agreement with conservative dates was good (CCC = 0.81 to 0.89).
items.author: Hackmann, T.

items.title: How Fisherian runaway halts: Genomic architecture determines the long-term evolutionary consequences of sexual selection.
items.summary: Sexual selection explains the evolution of exaggerated sexual displays, but less obvious is why biased mate preferences--a requirement for sexual selection--evolve. Fisher (1930) proposed that biased mate preferences can spark self-reinforcing evolutionary process (runaway) that drives their own evolution. This occurs because mate choice imposes sexual selection on sexual displays and links them genetically to mate preferences, producing indirect selection on the preferences themselves. While mathematical models have demonstrated the plausibility of the runaway theory, they rely on several idealized assumptions. Consequently, it remains poorly understood how runaway halts once populations deviate from these idealized conditions as a consequence of evolution via runaway, and how the genetic architecture underlying sexual displays influences the resulting evolutionary dynamics.

items.title: Saccadic suppression enhances saliency of ecologically relevant stimuli in the zebrafish optic tectum
items.summary: by Giulia Soto, Carina Thomas, Louis Funk, Tim C. Hladnik, Florian A. Dehmelt, Ziad M. Hafed, Aristides B. Arrenberg Saccadic suppression, a reduction in visual sensitivity around the time of rapid eye movements, is well-documented in primate psychophysics, but its mechanisms and functions remain debated. Here, we use zebrafish to trace the origins of saccadic suppression, and we demonstrate how saccadic suppression selectively enhances the visual salience of ecologically relevant stimuli. Saccadic suppression thus contributes to more than just compensation for rapid saccade-induced image shifts. We first established a behavioral correlate of saccadic suppression in larval zebrafish escape behavior. Then, using electrophysiology, we show that retinal ganglion cells jumpstart saccadic suppression in a spatial frequency-dependent manner.
