items.title: Patient-Reported Experiences of Long-Term Recovery and Persistent Psychosocial Burden in NMDAR Encephalitis.
items.summary: Background and objectives N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis is a rare autoimmune disorder with severe neuropsychiatric symptoms. Although neurologic recovery is often favorable, emerging evidence shows high prevalence of long-term sequelae affecting quality of life. Most studies rely on standardized assessments, leaving patient-reported experiences underexplored. We examined long-term psychosocial outcomes using a mixed-methods approach integrating patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), neuropsychological testing, and semistructured interviews informed by qualitative findings from SAPIENCE Level 1. Methods Sixty-five patients with NMDAR encephalitis were recruited across 3 centers (Berlin, Barcelona, and Lyon) at a median of 7.3 years postonset. Remote assessment included semistructured interviews, validated PROMs (sleep quality, fatigue, depression, anxiety, and quality of life), and neuropsychological testing.
items.author: Boeken OJ, Patricio V, Duda-Sikula M, Buttard C, Benaiteau M, Erazo L, Easton A, Papi C, Milano C, Kurpas D, Honnorat J, Dalmau JO, Finke C.

items.title: Pulmonary Vein Anatomy, Cooling Kinetics, and Recurrence After Cryoballoon Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
items.summary: Background Cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation depends on balloon-to-ostium contact. We assessed whether computed tomography-derived pulmonary vein ostial area (OA) and ovality index (OI) were associated with cooling after accounting for pulmonary vein (PV) branch and within-patient clustering, and whether PV anatomy was associated with recurrence. Methods We retrospectively studied 120 patients with symptomatic atrial fibrillation undergoing second-generation cryoballoon ablation. Vein-level associations with nadir temperature, 1 min temperature, and time to isolation were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with a patient random intercept and PV branch as a fixed effect; generalized estimating equations served as sensitivity analyses. Given 23 post-blanking recurrences, logistic models were limited to left atrial volume index (LAVI) and one clinically selected covariate, with Firth-penalized regression as a sensitivity analysis.
items.author: Yang KM, Hsiao HC, Yeh TC, Chiou CW, Hung JF, Chiang CH.

items.title: Multi-Environment Genomic Analysis Reveals Limited Concordance Between Sorghum Leaf Blight Incidence and Severity.
items.summary: Leaf blight caused by Exserohilum turcicum constrains sorghum production in semi-arid environments. Disease incidence and severity are related, but their relationship need not imply shared resistance loci. Records from five locations in Niger and Senegal comprised 1339 paired plot observations. Field-stratum-adjusted accession values were estimated before rank-based inverse-normal transformation. The primary population contained 100 accessions evaluated in at least four locations; all 102 genotype-matched accessions were included in a sensitivity analysis. Genome-wide efficient mixed-model association (GEMMA) score tests used leave-one-chromosome-out kinship matrices, and trait-level p -values were combined with the aggregated Cauchy association test (ACAT) and the Simes procedure. Adjusted incidence and standard severity were moderately correlated (Pearson r = 0.429); the correlation was lower after conditioning severity on incidence ( r = 0.066).
items.author: Ahn E, Baek I, Prom LK, Kim MS, Meinhardt LW, Magill C.

items.title: Education Research: Strengthening the Neurology Pipeline: The American Academy of Neurology Medical Student Symposium (2018-2025).
items.summary: Background and objectives The American Academy of Neurology (AAN) Medical Student Symposium (MSS) was established in 2018 to address the shortage of neurologists, with events consisting of keynote speakers, panel events, and networking opportunities to engage medical students with neurology. The aim of this study was to highlight the evolution of the MSS, to identify the elements participants perceived most beneficial, and to describe the longitudinal impact of the symposium on attendees. Methods We describe the MSS, recruitment processes, and its evolution from 2018 to 2025. To determine the longitudinal impact of the MSS on medical student interest in neurology, 1,177 attendees of past MSS were invited to participate in an online survey.
items.author: Fu KA, Soares CJ, Jordan JT, Geguera R, Urvig M, Posas J, Zelikovich AS, Day GS, Said RR.

items.title: Three-Dimensional Gait Analysis in STXBP1-Related Disorder.
items.summary: Background and objectives STXBP1-related disorder (STXBP1-RD), caused by pathogenic variants in the STXBP1 gene, is a rare neurodevelopmental condition, characterized by early-onset seizures, developmental delay, intellectual disability (ID), and prominent motor dysfunction. Despite the high prevalence of motor symptoms, systematic gait characterization remains limited. The aim of this study was therefore to quantitatively assess gait in participants with STXBP1-RD. Methods In this cross-sectional study, we included ambulatory participants aged 6 years or older with genetically confirmed STXBP1-RD. Instrumented 3D gait analysis (i3DGA) was performed to objectively quantify gait. Functional mobility was assessed with the Functional Mobility Scale (FMS) and Mobility Questionnaire 28 (MobQues28).
items.author: Swinnen M, Gys L, Thalwitzer KM, Deporte A, Van Gorp C, Vermeer E, Salami F, Weckhuysen S, Wolf SI, Syrbe S, Schoonjans AV, Hallemans A, Stamberger H.

items.title: Tonic neuron position and network topology determine synchronization dynamics.
items.summary: Understanding how collective neuronal rhythms emerge from the interplay between network structure and single-neuron dynamics remains a fundamental challenge in neurodynamics. In this work, we show that in small heterogeneous networks, the network topology and the position of a single tonic neuron govern synchronization dynamics. We study minimal four-neuron Huber-Braun motifs composed of one tonic neuron and three bursting neurons coupled via electrical synapses. By systematically varying the tonic neuron's centrality-quantified through degree and a quasi-Laplacian measure-we identify two critical coupling thresholds: the critical coupling for global phase synchronization and the coupling at which the network returns to synchronized periodic bursting.
items.author: Megchun AF, Padilla P, Espinal-Enríquez J, Santos GJE, Bernal-Jaquez R.

items.title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system.
items.summary: Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) has a wide range of etiologies, and the imaging differentiation between benign and ischemic PI is difficult, leading to a high risk of missed diagnosis. This study systematically summarizes the CT (Computed Tomography) imaging manifestations of PI and constructs an AI (Artificial Intelligence)-assisted diagnostic model that integrates multidimensional features. This study retrospectively collected CT and x-ray data from 612 patients with PI (398 benign and 214 ischemic cases) from three tertiary hospitals, and included an external validation set of 106 cases. Imaging analysis established a five-level PI-CT severity scoring system based on gas morphology, distribution, portal venous gas (PVG), intestinal wall enhancement, mesenteric edema, and ascites.
items.author: Zhang X.

items.title: Gfi1ab-Cebpβ axis promotes eosinophilopoiesis in zebrafish.
items.summary: Eosinophils play essential roles in parasite defense, allergic responses, and tissue homeostasis, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing their development remain incompletely understood. GFI1 is an important regulator of multiple hematopoietic lineages, but its role in eosinophil development is unclear. Using zebrafish as a model, we demonstrate that Gfi1ab promotes eosinophil development, as gfi1ab mutation significantly reduces eosinophil numbers, whereas its overexpression enhances eosinophilopoiesis. This effect is probably eosinophil-specific, as gfi1ab mutation does not significantly affect erythrocyte, neutrophil, or macrophage development. Integrative RNA-Seq and Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-Seq) analyses identify cebpb as a potential downstream target of Gfi1ab. Mechanistically, gfi1ab deficiency reduces cebpb expression, and cebpb overexpression partially rescues the eosinophil defects in gfi1ab -deficient larvae.
items.author: Wen H, Hu Z, Wu M, Peng W, Sun Y, Li J, Lian J, Huang Y, Zhang Y, Li G.

items.title: Associations between psychiatric comorbidity and intensive care unit length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality: A retrospective observational study.
items.summary: Aim Psychiatric comorbidities are common among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), but findings regarding their impact on clinical outcomes remain inconsistent. Additionally, existing studies have often included patients admitted for suicide attempts or self-harm, leaving insufficient evidence about the independent effects of psychiatric comorbidity on clinical outcomes. To address this gap, this study investigated the independent association of psychiatric comorbidity with ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, and in-hospital mortality among patients admitted to the ICU, excluding those admitted for suicide attempts or self-harm. Methods Of the 2599 patients admitted to the ICU of a university hospital, 2192 were included in the analysis.
items.author: Nakamura T, Momma T, Yoshizawa T, Arai Y, Sasayama D, Mita A, Imamura H, Hashimoto R, Washizuka S.

items.title: Azole resistance among clinical Aspergillus fumigatus species complex isolates in Greece: first detection of TR 46 -mediated resistance and azole-resistant cryptic species.
items.summary: Objectives To assess the prevalence of antifungal resistance among clinical Aspergillus fumigatus species complex (SC) isolates in Greece, focusing on azole resistance and its underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A total of 249 clinical A. fumigatus SC isolates were collected from geographically distinct centres across Greece. Antifungal susceptibility testing (AFST) was conducted according to EUCAST guidelines. Cryptic species and azole-resistant A. fumigatus (AR Af ) isolates underwent confirmatory molecular identification. AR Af sensu stricto ( SS ) isolates were further analysed by CYP51A gene and promoter sequencing to detect resistance-associated mutations. Results Most isolates (246/249; 99%) were identified as A. fumigatus SS , while three isolates were molecularly identified as A.
items.author: Siopi M, Vargiami M, Beredaki MI, Velegraki A, Zachariadou L, Roilides E, Chamilos G, Antonopoulou S, Skoura L, Alastruey-Izquierdo A, Pournaras S, Meletiadis J.

items.title: Contextualizing a One Health definition of appropriate antimicrobial use.
items.summary: Background and objectives Antimicrobial stewardship initiatives are designed to improve the appropriateness of antimicrobial use and thereby maximize benefits and minimize risks. Currently, there is no shared understanding of appropriate use. Qualitative research with key stakeholders in human and animal health is critical to inform a One Health definition and to support global stewardship efforts. Methods Four qualitative focus groups were held in 2024 with livestock producers, consumers, healthcare professionals and policymakers to examine factors affecting antimicrobial use and stewardship. A thematic analysis methodology informed by grounded theory was adopted, capturing themes as they emerged directly from the data. Results Thematic analysis identified two themes:Structural and economic barriers; in animal health, consumer demand for free-range or antibiotic-free produce conflicted with practical antimicrobial use.
items.author: Schermuly A, Scarborough R, Dowson L, Teoh L, Biezen R, Bailey K, Hur B, McMullan B, Ierano C, Hardefeldt L.

items.title: Amikacin activity against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae without phenotypic aminoglycoside resistance: impact of aminoglycoside-modifying enzyme (AME) gene aac(6')-Ib-cr in vitro and in vivo .
items.summary: Objectives Aminoglycosides are often combined with β-lactams for the treatment of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, but the impact of aminoglycoside-modifying enzyme (AME) genes on treatment efficacy in phenotypically susceptible isolates remains unclear. We evaluated whether aac(6')-Ib-cr , the AME gene with recognized activity against amikacin, attenuates amikacin efficacy in KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae . Methods Thirteen clinical isolates of KPC-producing K. pneumoniae without phenotypic aminoglycoside resistance (amikacin MIC ≤4 mg/L; median 2, range 0.5-3 mg/L) were studied. Three were AME-negative; 10 were AME-positive, carrying aac(6')-Ib-cr , aac(3)-IIa and strA/strB . Amikacin activity was assessed by time-kill assays and a Galleria mellonella survival model, compared with ceftazidime-avibactam.
items.author: Kim J, Seong JE, Lee YJ, Park S, Han M, Lee Y, Lee JA, Kim JH, Ahn JY, Jeong SJ, Ku NS, Yeom JS, Lee H, Choi JY.

items.title: Global burden of chronic kidney disease attributable to hypertension due to high body mass index: projections to 2050.
items.summary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 9.1% of the global population, equivalent to approximately 843 million individuals as of 2021, with hypertension (HTN) as a major contributor. High body mass index (BMI) exacerbates HTN-related kidney injury, but the global burden of HTN-related CKD attributable to high BMI remains poorly characterized. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study for 1990-2021, we estimated attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and the age-standardized disability-adjusted life-year rate (ASDR). Temporal trends were assessed using the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), and a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was used to project rates to 2050.
items.author: Li L, Zhu G, Wang KK, Maimaiti S, Wang S, Lu C.

items.title: Association between pancreatic ectopic fat deposition and QCT-assessed bone mass status in patients with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study.
items.summary: Background Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of bone abnormalities. Beyond disturbances in mineral metabolism, ectopic fat deposition may also be associated with skeletal abnormalities in CKD. However, the relationship between pancreatic fat and bone mass status remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between mean pancreatic fat fraction and quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-assessed bone mass status in patients with CKD. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 327 patients with CKD. Vertebral volumetric bone mineral density was measured using QCT to classify bone mass status as normal bone mass, osteopenia, or osteoporosis. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was quantified from CT images.
items.author: Yang J, Wang R, Xue G, Wei J, Wang L.

items.title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
items.summary: Background Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA. Methods This randomized controlled trial enrolled young women with IDA aged 18-25 years, who were randomly assigned to a training group (TG; n = 16) or a non-training group (NTG; n = 17).
items.author: Harrabi MA, Fendri T, Ayed R, Boughattas W, Chaari F, Mezghani I, Kallel C, Rebai H, Turki M, Ayadi F, Sahli S.

items.title: Extended DNA damage-induced G2/M arrests lead to aberrant mitoses through accumulation of securin.
items.summary: The stochastic nature of DNA damage dictates various scenarios of stress survival among different cells. We used time-lapse microscopy to perform single-cell level analyses of yeast populations with double-stranded DNA breaks and nonfunctional telomeres. Activation of the DNA damage signalling resulted in a broad distribution in the duration of G2/M arrests. Strikingly, the longer arrests correlated with aberrant mitoses caused by miscoordination of nuclear division and cytokinesis, leading to cell death. Chk1-dependent phosphorylation of Pds1 (securin), an inhibitor of sister chromatid separation in mitosis, was responsible for this phenomenon. Securin progressively accumulated during G2/M arrests, leading to grossly delayed or missed nuclear divisions.
items.author: Dubenko A, Jnied M, Kotenko O, Makovets S.

items.title: Configurational patterns associated with relatively higher recent home-based exercise behavior among lung transplant recipients: a fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis.
items.summary: Background Home-based exercise supports functional recovery after lung transplantation, yet exercise behavior varies among recipients. Guided by the capability, opportunity, motivation, and behavior (COM-B) model, this study examined configurations associated with relatively higher recent home-based exercise behavior among lung transplant recipients. Methods This cross-sectional study included adult lung transplant recipients within the first year after transplantation at a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang, China. Five COM-B-related conditions were assessed: 6-min walk distance, exercise rehabilitation knowledge, perceived social support, exercise self-efficacy, and exercise automaticity. Recent home-based exercise behavior during the previous 7 days was assessed through structured retrospective interviews and calculated as MET-min/week.
items.author: Zhu Q, Tang L, Lin P, Zeng F, Lan M.

items.title: Associations of fetal growth patterns and growth in the first two years of life: a longitudinal study of a Beijing birth cohort.
items.summary: Background This study aimed to evaluate the association between fetal growth patterns and early childhood growth rate. Methods In total, 6,370 mother-child pairs were included in a birth cohort in Beijing. Fetal biometric parameters were measured at 20-24, 28-32, 33-36 weeks, and at ≥37 weeks of gestation, and infant weight and length were assessed from birth to 24 months of age. Changes in the weight-for-length Z-score (WLZ) from birth to 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, and 24 months of age were used to classify infant growth velocity as slow (change in WLZ 0.67). A group-based trajectory model was used to identify fetal growth patterns.
items.author: Meng X, Li X, Yi L, Xiong X, Zhong S, Wu M, Zhang N, Wu Q.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of recombinant influenza vaccine compared with standard-dose influenza vaccine among adults 50 years of age and older in Hong Kong.
items.summary: Older adults face a disproportionately high risk of severe influenza, yet the standard inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV) offers suboptimal protection in this population. This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of replacing IIV with the recombinant influenza vaccine (RIV) for adults aged ≥50, ≥65, and ≥80 years in Hong Kong. We used a decision tree model to compare RIV with IIV for adults aged ≥50, ≥65, and ≥80 years in Hong Kong, from a societal perspective. Costs, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were evaluated, and the impact of parameter uncertainty on the results was assessed via deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses.
items.author: Zhong S, Wong IOL, Wu P, Cowling BJ.

items.title: Pharmacological treatment of bereavement-related distress: a systematic review.
items.summary: Background: With the recent addition of prolonged grief disorder into diagnostic manuals both in the United States (i.e. DSM-5-TR) and internationally (i.e. ICD-11), interest in pharmacologic treatment for grief has increased. Objective: Here, we review how bereavement-related psychological distress, including treating depression secondary to bereavement, has been addressed pharmacologically and the efficacy of these treatments. Methods: Included studies focused on (1) patients bereaved by any cause, (2) patients suffering from bereavement-related mental health problems, and (3) pharmacotherapy interventions to treat those bereavement-related mental health problems. Six databases (MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, APA PsycInfo, Scopus, and Web of Science) were searched on 1 October 2020, and updated through 18 December 2024.
items.author: LaPlante CD, Saviano SC, Hardt MM, Pain K, Kolla S, Lee C, Maciejewski PK, Russell D, Smid GE, Prigerson HG.

items.title: Psychosocial pathways linking PTSD and DSO symptoms to somatic symptoms among female North Korean defectors.
items.summary: Background: North Korean defectors (NKDs), approximately 72% of whom are female, are a trauma-exposed population in which somatic symptoms are common and culturally patterned. Previous research identified loneliness, perceived discrimination, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and disturbances in self-organization (DSO) symptoms as correlates of somatic symptoms. However, whether loneliness and perceived discrimination account for these relationships remains unclear. Objective: To examine whether loneliness and perceived discrimination mediate the relationship between PTSD/DSO symptoms and somatic symptoms among female NKDs. Methods: This secondary analysis used cross-sectional survey data from 372 female NKDs in South Korea. PTSD and DSO symptom severity were assessed using the International Trauma Questionnaire.
items.author: Kim H, Kim O, Chu SH.

items.title: Understanding posttraumatic growth after suicide bereavement: the impact of coping style and reflective functioning.
items.summary: Background: The experience of suicide bereavement (SB) may vary when compared to expected bereavement (EB) and unexpected bereavement (UB). However, evidence has shown that individuals bereaved by suicide can experience posttraumatic growth (PTG). Additionally, other research has highlighted that one's coping style and level of reflective functioning (RF) can impact trauma response. Understanding the impact of these factors could enhance support for those in need. Objective: This study had three objectives: (1) Investigate the relationship between RF and PTG in the context of bereavement for emerging adults; (2) Compare PTG experience following EB, UB, and SB; (3) Examine the relationship between RF and coping style in relation to PTG in this population (i.e.
items.author: Whittaker S, Tse DCK, Rasmussen S, Cogan N, Shiramizu V.

items.title: Personality structure mediates the impact of childhood adversity on psychopathology in adolescents with personality disorder.
items.summary: Background: Personality disorders (PD) emerge in adolescence, a developmentally vulnerable period notable for emotional instability and high risk-taking behaviour. After decades of reluctance to diagnose PD in adolescence, early diagnosis and intervention are now called for. Patients present with severe psychopathology including heightened suicide risk. It is important to investigate underlying mechanisms for informed treatment planning. Childhood adversities (CA) are thought to play a key role in developing a PD. Objective: We aimed to deepen our understanding of the mechanism linking CA to psychopathology including suicidality in adolescent PD. Method: In 113 adolescents (mean age 15.6 (SD 1.23), 79 patients and 34 healthy controls), PD was dimensionally assessed using the Structured Interview for Personality Organisation, adapted to the adolescent language (STIPO-R-A), which encompasses identity, interpersonal relationships, defence mechanisms and coping strategies, level of aggression, and moral functioning.
items.author: Czernin K, Bründlmayer A, Zeiler M, Bangerl W, Krischer M, Laczkovics C.

items.title: Caregiver-Reported Signs and Symptoms of Autonomic Dysfunction in Koolen-de Vries Syndrome.
items.summary: Objective To evaluate whether autonomic signs and symptoms are overrepresented in people with Koolen-de Vries syndrome (KdVS). Methods In this observational study, individuals with KdVS and their caregivers were recruited at an international advocacy summit and through social media invitations facilitated by the KdVS Foundation. Caregivers of people with KdVS completed the Pediatric Autonomic Symptoms Scale (PASS) questionnaire and were invited to provide anecdotal reports of their experiences with possible autonomic dysfunction. Data were compared with previously published cohorts of healthy controls, individuals with familial dysautonomia (FD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), or nonspecific neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD). Results Thirty-seven individuals with KdVS participated.
items.author: Sahly AN, Rampakakis E, Myers KA.

items.title: Cryptic Presentations of Neurologic Wilson Disease With ATP7B Peptide Assessments.
items.summary: Objectives To illustrate the phenotypic variability in neurologic Wilson disease (NWD) and diagnostic value of ATP7B peptide testing in resolving WD cases. Methods We conducted a case series analysis of 3 individuals with suspected NWD. Clinical presentation, diagnostic workup including traditional biomarkers, genetic testing, and ATP7B peptide quantification by immuno-selected reaction monitoring mass spectrometry were reviewed. Results The 3 patients demonstrated diverse neurologic presentations: (1) an adult with coexisting Parkinson disease and WD, exhibiting parkinsonian features with partial response to dopaminergic therapy; (2) a child with early-onset dystonia and neuropsychiatric symptoms; and (3) an adult initially misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis.
items.author: Penon-Portmann M, Tapia C, Patterson KC, Beckman E, Zhang JG, Chen-Deutsch X, Shelkowitz E, Larson A, Duong P, Grotzer T, Valentino PL, Davis MY, Hahn S.

items.title: 2025 Peds Day Presentations
Primary Tracheal Lymphoma Mimicking Asthma Exacerbation.
items.summary: A 88-year-old woman with refractory wheezing and a transient response to corticosteroids was diagnosed with primary tracheal B-cell lymphoma causing airway stenosis. Emergency radiotherapy markedly improved the stenosis. Tracheal lymphoma should be considered in patients with recurrent wheezing despite asthma treatment, even when corticosteroids provide temporary relief.
items.author: Uchimura K, Kitajima S, Hirai M, Ishida T.

items.title: Dynamic Resource Partitioning in a Marine Predator Community.
items.summary: To avoid competition, species partition resource-use along various niche axes. However, variable resource availability, especially within dynamic environments, may influence this partitioning. Theory predicts that species will contract their ecological niche to limit competition during times of resource scarcity. We analysed blood δ 13 C and δ 15 N composition in four albatrosses, four penguin, two giant petrel and two fur seal species breeding on sub-Antarctic Marion Island, during two seasons (autumn and summer) over 3 years. Using the species' seasonal stable isotopic niche space as a proxy for trophic niche space, we investigated their trophic dynamics and maintenance of inter-specific resource partitioning.
items.author: Carpenter-Kling T, Connan M, Reisinger RR, Makhado AB, Ryan PG, Pistorius PA.

items.title: Spotted Patterns of Glass Frogs Can Disguise Imperfections in Transparency to Improve Camouflage.
items.summary: Transparency could be considered the idealized version of camouflage, capable of producing effective concealment across heterogeneous habitats. However, although examples of highly transparent species do exist, 'transparent' species are highly variable and are often either only partially transparent or better described as translucent. Exactly how these different forms of 'imperfect' transparency may act as camouflage remains largely unknown. The glass frogs (Centrolenidae) have long been thought of as a classic example of transparent camouflage due to their see-through ventral skin. Yet even in these seemingly exemplary cases, glass frogs are better described as translucent due to the presence of obligate opaque structures, such as the internal organs, within the body and opaque color patterns in their dorsal skin.
items.author: Yeager J, Ávila L, Barnett JB.

items.title: Persistent Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) in Patients With Malignant Lymphoma Treated With Anti-CD20 Antibodies Who Responded to Ensitrelvir: A Report of Three Cases.
items.summary: Patients with malignant lymphoma receiving anti-CD20 antibody therapy are at high risk of persistent coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), with no established standard treatment. We report three cases of persistent COVID-19 in patients with follicular lymphoma who responded clinically after switching to ensitrelvir following the failure of remdesivir-based treatment. Each patient had multiple relapses and an inadequate response to remdesivir but achieved symptom resolution with ensitrelvir. These cases suggest that switching to an antiviral with a different mechanism of action may be an effective therapeutic strategy for immunocompromised patients when initial antiviral therapies fail.
items.author: Horie M, Okimoto T, Okada Y, Inoue M, Shimizu S, Tsuda H, Hata K, Okuno T, Amano Y, Nakao M, Nakashima K, Hamaguchi M, Isobe T.

items.title: Characteristics of Professionals Involved in Open Science in Ecology and Evolution .
items.summary: Open science aims to improve research transparency, reuse and societal impact, yet its adoption and reach ultimately depend on people. Understanding how personal characteristics such as gender, work experience or professional role influence familiarity with, attitudes toward and engagement in open science is critical for the effective, widespread implementation of open science practices. We surveyed 342 individuals who produce, mobilise or use scientific knowledge in ecology and evolutionary biology. Their engagement was analysed using the open science change framework, which conceptualises open science as a progression from familiarity and perceptions to practices and support for societal goals, as outlined in the UNESCO Recommendations.
items.author: Zagrodzka ZB, Johnson TF, Beckerman AP.

items.title: Mapping Leopard Conservation Priorities in Southeast Asia.
items.summary: The Indochinese leopard ( Panthera pardus delacouri ) is one of the most endangered leopard subspecies, restricted to < 4% of its historical range across Southeast Asia. With severe declines driven by poaching, habitat loss and fragmentation, and prey depletion, recovery requires urgent, spatially informed conservation action. This study presents the first connectivity analysis for the Indochinese leopard across its extant and former range, aiming to identify core habitats, priority connectivity areas and opportunities for population restoration. We used resistant kernel modelling through the CoLa Decision Support System to evaluate landscape connectivity across 14 forest complexes in the extant range and 11 potential reintroduction areas, considering scenarios of extant, reintroduction and combined range connectivity.
items.author: Atzeni L, Kamler J, Ash E, Kyaw PP, Rasphone A, Pin C, Tan CKW, Rostro-García S, Jantz P, Gonzalez I, Burnham D, Cushman SA, Macdonald DW.

items.title: Retraction: Association Between Mucosal Cytomegalovirus DNA Load and Short-Term Clinical Outcomes in Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis.
items.summary: [This retracts the article DOI: 10.7759/cureus.113063.].
items.author: Bassi N, Yadav D, Ghoshal UC, Dixit VK, Ghoshal U, Kumar V, Tiwari AK, Malakar S, Shah AS, Mittal I, Parihar SP, Mahajan M, Bansal M, Singla A.

items.title: Arthroscopic Scapholunate Osseous Ligament Anchor-Based Round-Block Repair for Scapholunate Instability.
items.summary: Scapholunate instability remains difficult to treat, particularly in lesions involving detachment of the dorsal intercarpal ligament from the scaphoid. We describe the Scapholunate Osseous Ligament Anchor-based Round-block technique, an arthroscopic anchor-based repair designed to reinsert and retension the dorsal capsuloligamentous complex. The procedure allows dynamic assessment of reduction and may be combined with additional palmar stabilization when needed. This modular technique may represent a useful arthroscopic option for selected patterns of scapholunate instability.
items.author: de Villeneuve Bargemon JB, Goorens CK, Merlini L, Audiffret L.

items.title: Arthroscopic Biologic Meniscal Root Repair With Iliotibial Band Autograft Augmentation.
items.summary: This paper presents a description of a surgical technique-a modified Henning-Piontek procedure-used for meniscal root salvage. The method is intended for difficult, chronic injuries with loss of continuity of the meniscal root. Such cases would most often result in total or subtotal meniscectomy, which, as is well known, significantly accelerates the degenerative changes in the knee. This technique aligns with the "save the meniscus" approach practiced and promoted by the authors. It involves the use of an iliotibial band graft to create a bridge between the damaged meniscus and the anatomical attachment site of the meniscal root. This enables anatomical repair of the meniscal root, facilitates healing, and preserves the natural structure of the joint.
items.author: Piontek T, Rubczak S, Bulinski P, Naczk J, Głowacki J, Bąbik B, Banach A.

items.title: More Than Color: Floral Color Polymorphism Is Associated With Scent Differentiation and Pollination Success in the Deceptive Orchid Anacamptis pyramidalis .
items.summary: Floral color polymorphism is widespread among flowering plants, yet the mechanisms underlying its maintenance remain poorly understood, particularly in food-deceptive orchids where pollinator-mediated selection may differ from that operating in rewarding species. Here, we investigated the relationship among floral color polymorphism, ploidy variation, floral scent composition, and pollination in the Mediterranean deceptive orchid Anacamptis pyramidalis . Cytotypes were determined by flow cytometry, and floral volatile organic compounds (VOCs) were analyzed using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) in white- and pink-flowered individuals from multiple populations. VOC profiles were compared using multivariate and univariate statistical approaches. Pollination success was assessed in mixed-color diploid and tetraploid populations by quantifying the number of mature fruits produced per individual.
items.author: Sasso M, Cafasso D, Romano VA, Brandt K, Ayasse M, Cozzolino S.

items.title: Insights into the effect of exposed Mn 2 O 3 crystal planes on toluene oxidation over MnO x /IM monolithic catalysts.
items.summary: In situ growth of Mn 2 O 3 on the surface of the iron mesh was performed hydrothermally to prepare novel catalysts with enhanced toluene oxidation performance. The effect of exposed crystal planes of catalysts, regulated by manganese concentration, on the catalytic performance of toluene oxidation was systematically studied using various characterization techniques, including XRD, SEM, TEM, Raman, H 2 -TPR, and XPS. The 1.2MnO x /IM catalyst exhibited superior toluene oxidation performance, attributed to Mn 2 O 3 (111)- facet-induced synergistic effects between its super-low-temperature oxidation capability and abundant oxygen vacancies. DFT calculations indicated that the catalyst with an exposed Mn 2 O 3 (111) crystal plane has stronger toluene/O 2 adsorption and weaker CO 2 adsorption, demonstrating its excellent catalytic activity and stability.
items.author: Huang K, Wang J, Zhao G, Gui X, Liu D, Gui J.

items.title: Open-Wedge High Tibial Osteotomy With Complete Tibial Tubercle Osteotomy to Preserve Patellar Height.
items.summary: Distalization of the tibial tubercle is a concern during open-wedge high tibial osteotomy, particularly when a large correction is required, considering the potential for patella baja and patellofemoral problems. This Technical Note describes the use of open-wedge high tibial osteotomy combined with complete tibial tubercle osteotomy to maintain the position of the tibial tubercle during correction. Performing tibial tubercle osteotomy first allows placement of a thin retractor beneath the fragment during the transverse osteotomy, helping to protect the fragment and reduce the risk of an incomplete osteotomy. Temporary fixation of the tibial tubercle to the proximal tibial fragment before wedge opening is a key step in maintaining the original position of the tubercle and preventing distalization during correction.
items.author: Miyasaka T, Kayama T, Kubota D, Arakawa S, Saito M.

items.title: Nanoimprinted Infrared Metasurface Multispectral Filters for Neural-Network-Assisted Low-Temperature Sensing.
items.summary: Low-temperature infrared sensing requires temperature information to be extracted from weak thermal radiation while preserving optical throughput. Nanoimprinted metasurface filters combine multispectral encoding with neural-network calibration to address this challenge. A single circular-ring geometry controls passband position, bandwidth, and overlap, with simulated tuning across 6.4-11.2 μm. Deep-ultraviolet stepper lithography and ultraviolet nanoimprinting transfer reusable master patterns to 1-inch zinc sulfide filters. Four broad, partially overlapping bands retain peak transmittance near 80% and provide complementary spectral inputs for blackbody measurements from -20°C to 20°C. Neural-network regression on the processed calibration curves achieves a mean absolute error of 0.160°C, compared with 0.434°C for one unfiltered input, a reduction of approximately 63%.
items.author: Yang S, Su Z, Dan Y.

items.title: Off-Label use of a lumen-apposing metal stent for refractory pyloric stricture in a toddler.
items.author: Khan HH, Wali P, Inamdar S.

items.title: Quantum Thermodynamic Transformation Optics: A Unified Framework for Energy and Entropy With Application to the Casimir Force in Dissipative Metamaterials.
items.summary: A novel concept, quantum thermodynamic transformation optics (QTTO), is introduced as a theoretical framework integrating transformation optics with thermodynamics of quantum dissipative systems. Beyond conventional coordinate transformations, QTTO describes how physically implemented transformation-optical media with dispersion, loss, reservoir noise, and boundary conditions reorganize the statistical distribution of quantum energy and entropy-related field fluctuations. Using thermofield dynamics, we establish transformation rules showing how local fluctuation related energy and entropy densities are controlled by the Jacobian determinant of the mapping. Geometric compression enhances local statistical weight of quantum and thermal fluctuations, whereas expansion produces the opposite effect, with global conservation laws and the second law of thermodynamics preserved.
items.author: Sadeghi MM, Sarısaman M.

items.title: Giant Lipoma of the Thoracic Wall in a Two-Year-Old Girl: Imaging Features Supporting a Benign Diagnosis.
items.summary: Lipomas are the most common mesenchymal neoplasms of soft tissue, but giant lipomas, defined as lesions exceeding 10 cm in any dimension or weighing more than 1 kg, are rare in young children, in whom lipoblastoma is the main adipocytic differential diagnosis and liposarcoma must be excluded. We report the case of a two-year-old girl with a left dorsal thoracic wall mass that had grown progressively over 18 months. A biopsy performed elsewhere one year earlier had shown mature adipose tissue without atypia. Radiography showed a large soft-tissue density mass with rib deformity, a sixth-rib fracture, and superior displacement of the scapula.
items.author: Da Silva Eli G, Rizon M, Bartolamei Ramos AA.

items.title: The role of soot oxidation on the optimization of chitosan/soot aerogel beads for heavy metals and dyes adsorption.
items.summary: The development of sustainable, shape-stable, and tunable adsorbents is a key challenge for water remediation, especially when pollutants differ in charge, structure, and adsorption mechanism. In this work, flame-generated soot particles were upcycled as carbonaceous fillers in crosslinked chitosan-based aerogel beads for the removal of two chemically distinct model contaminants: hexavalent chromium, Cr(vi), and Rhodamine 6G (R6G). Pristine and nitric-acid-oxidized soot were incorporated into the chitosan matrix at different ratios to investigate how the filler surface chemistry and the aerogel composition affect the adsorption performance. The resulting nanocomposite aerogels retained a porous bead morphology and displayed pH-dependent adsorption behavior. Cr(vi) removal was favored by chitosan-rich formulations under acidic conditions (highest experimental adsorption capacity around 75 mg g -1 obtained with the CS : soot-ox 2 : 1 sample at 40 °C), consistently with the role of protonated chitosan sites in attracting anionic chromate species.
items.author: Ahmad S, Maroulas KN, Sirignano M, Salzano de Luna M, Kyzas GZ.

items.title: Broadscale Distribution and Pronounced Mitochondrial Phylogeographic Structure in the Freshwater Minnow Opsariichthys bidens Across China's Major River Basins.
items.summary: China's complex river basins constitute a critical biogeographic setting for investigating genetic differentiation and lineage divergence in freshwater fishes. Opsariichthys bidens is broadly distributed among multiple, hydrologically isolated river basins, rendering it a well-suited system for assessing mitochondrial phylogeographic structure across major river basins. Here, we used newly generated mitochondrial data to characterize broad-scale genetic variation in O. bidens across China's major river basins. We analyzed 379 cytochrome b ( cyt b ) sequences sampled from 13 geographically distinct populations, including seven populations from the Yangtze River and one population from each of six other major rivers, complemented by complete mitochondrial genomes from one individual from each population.
items.author: Wang X, Yin D, Liu J, Yan M, Li W, Liu S, Jiang M, Sun N, Liu K, Yan Y.

items.title: Visible-light-driven synthesis of quinazoline derivatives using a recyclable CuO/TiO 2 nanocomposite photocatalyst.
items.summary: A visible-light-driven photocatalytic protocol was developed for the synthesis of diverse quinazoline derivatives using a recyclable CuO/TiO 2 nanocomposite as a heterogeneous catalyst. Characterization by XRD, FT-IR, FE-SEM, and UV-Vis DRS confirmed the successful fabrication of the composite with enhanced visible-light absorption. Under blue-LED irradiation and ambient air, the CuO/TiO 2 catalyst effectively mediated the cascade oxidation of 2-aminobenzyl alcohol to 2-aminobenzaldehyde, followed by condensation with benzaldehydes and an ammonia source to afford a broad scope of quinazolines in good to excellent isolated yields (89-96%). Radical-trapping experiments demonstrated that superoxide radical species (O 2 ˙ - ) and photogenerated holes (h + ) play pivotal roles in the catalytic transformation.
items.author: Hoseinshahi DZ, Hassankhani A, Akbari A, Lashkari B.

items.title: All-Inside Posterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using Achilles Allograft and Suture Tape Augmentation.
items.summary: Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) reconstruction is challenged by graft elongation and delayed biological integration, often necessitating slow rehabilitation and carrying a risk of arthrofibrosis. This technical report describes an all-inside technique augmented with the modified internal bracing to address these limitations. The technique involves integrating a FiberTape within a quadrupled Achilles tendon allograft, creating a load-sharing composite. An all-inside, retrograde socket method was used for anatomic PCL reconstruction in the knee, with suspensory fixation on both femur and tibia. The graft-tape construct was simultaneously tensioned. The technique provides immediate biomechanical stability by mitigating graft micromotion, elongation, and tunnel abrasion. By closely replicating native PCL stiffness, this construct facilitates an accelerated, protective rehabilitation protocol focused on early motion and quadriceps activation, thereby aiming to reduce failure rates and postoperative stiffness.
items.author: Md Yusoff BAH, Zhafri A, Ramlan MKR, Nik Kamaruzman NKA, Omar A, Mohamad N, Azwan Aziz M.

items.title: KRAS G12Y Causing a False-Positive KRAS G12C Result With an Indistinguishable PCR Pattern in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
items.summary: KRAS G12C is an actionable alteration in non-small cell lung cancer, making accurate molecular identification essential for treatment selection. A 61-year-old man with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma showed a KRAS G12C-positive reaction on the AmoyDx Pan Lung Cancer PCR Panel (AmoyDx PLC panel). After progression on first-line chemoimmunotherapy, sotorasib was administered, but progressive disease was observed at the first radiologic assessment. Subsequent NGS-based comprehensive genomic profiling of the same pretreatment FFPE block identified KRAS G12Y (c.34_35delinsTA; variant allele frequency, 25.8%), with no sequence reads supporting KRAS G12C. This prompted suspicion of a false-positive PCR result. Repeat AmoyDx PLC panel testing reproduced the G12C-positive reaction and testing of a KRAS G12Y plasmid likewise yielded a G12C-positive reaction without additional KRAS-associated signals, confirming cross-reactivity.
items.author: Iwasaki T, Ikushima H, Nakamura M, Mikami Y, Watanabe K, Kawakami M, Mitani A, Kage H.

items.title: A Rare Endobronchial Lipoma of the Right Middle Lobe Causing Middle Lobe Syndrome and Recurrent Post-Obstructive Infection in a Patient With Interstitial Lung Disease, Managed by Lung-Sparing Bronchoscopy.
items.summary: Endobronchial lipomas are rare benign tumours that can cause airway obstruction and recurrent infection. A 70-year-old smoker with combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema presented with recurrent right middle lobe infections and declining pulmonary function. Computed tomography revealed a fat-density lesion obstructing the middle lobe bronchus, with atelectasis and consolidation. Bronchoscopy and histology confirmed lipoma. Given limited respiratory reserve, lung-sparing flexible bronchoscopy with snare electrocautery and argon plasma coagulation restored airway patency; retained purulent secretions were drained and infection treated. At 2 months, the patient was asymptomatic with radiological resolution; FVC improved from 75% to 83% predicted and DLCO from 35% to 50% predicted.
items.author: Palamidas A, Papatheodosiou K, Karagianni E, Daglis F, Bouros D.

items.title: Respiratory oscillometry findings in World Trade Center-exposed rescue/recovery workers.
items.summary: Background Persistent respiratory symptoms are common in Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) rescue/recovery workers following the World Trade Center (WTC) collapse on 11 September 2001 and some continue to experience symptoms despite normal spirometry without bronchodilator response. Respiratory oscillometry is a sensitive method for detecting small airways dysfunction and identifies abnormalities undetected by spirometry. This study evaluated whether respiratory oscillometry is associated with respiratory symptoms among workers with normal spirometry, and qualitatively assessed this association stratified by serum eosinophilia. Methods We analysed a cohort of FDNY WTC-exposed rescue/recovery workers who completed same-day respiratory oscillometry, spirometry and symptom questionnaires.
items.author: Cleven KL, Zeig-Owens R, Goldfarb DG, Vaeth BM, Galfund J, Weiden MD, Berger KI, Prezant DJ.

items.title: Remote Sensing for Operational Surveillance of Mosquito-Borne Diseases.
items.summary: Remote sensing observations have demonstrated increasing value in identifying human risk from mosquito-borne diseases because mosquito ecology is intrinsically tied to geophysical variables measurable by satellites. Satellite-based monitoring of environmental conditions at varying temporal and spatial scales has extended our capacity for mosquito surveillance and control for many mosquito-borne diseases, including malaria, dengue, Zika, West Nile fever, and Rift Valley fever. However, technical challenges and operational limitations continue to pose barriers for more routine integration of satellite data into management programs. To achieve this, we need to more explicitly connect these technologies to practical management scales, which are often disconnected from the spatial and temporal scales at which remote sensing data are readily accessible.
items.author: Ash LV, Willard LL, Harrod KK, Tucker CJ, Linthicum KJ, Anyamba A, Gibson S, Han BA, Kramer AM.

items.title: Resource Availability Shaped the Female-Biased Floral Sex Allocation With Plant Size in Andromonoecious Capparis spinosa in Desert.
items.summary: Although classic models of size-dependent sex allocation (SDS) generally predict that among animal-pollinated plants, female allocation increases with individual size, male-and female-biased allocation patterns have also been reported. We hypothesized that Capparis spinosa growing in resource-poor desert habitats would exhibit a female-biased sex allocation with increasing plant size, and that this pattern would be directly regulated by resource availability, because female function is generally more resource-demanding to verify this conjecture. We examined SDS patterns at the flowering stage in the andromonoecious desert plant C. spinosa and assessed the role of resource availability in shaping these patterns through resource supplementation and pruning treatments.
items.author: Cai YJ, Lu Y, Abdusalam A.

items.title: Studying the structure-property relationship in Zr-BDI MOF for noble-metal-free selective photocatalytic CO 2 conversion to CO.
items.summary: Photocatalytic conversion of CO 2 to value-added products by metal-organic framework (MOF)-based catalysts often requires the introduction of secondary metal sites or the anchoring of noble-metal-based photosensitizers, leading to complex designs and increased costs. In this work, we focus on the structure-property relationship of MOFs, emphasizing the band gap and conduction band position of the MOF catalyst. Here, we use a light-sensitive linker [ N , N '-di(3,5-dicarboxyphenyl)benzene tetracarboxylic diimide] to design a robust, intrinsically photo-redox-active zirconium MOF. This Zr-MOF with scu topology has a band gap of 2.84 eV and a conduction band position of -0.64 V vs. NHE, which is well positioned for the conversion of CO 2 to CO without the addition of noble metal atoms or photosensitizers.
items.author: Chandran P A, Verma TS, Sarkar S, Chanda A, Assen AH, Nag A, Babarao R, Roy S, Aggarwal H.

items.title: A molecular networking-guided strategy for identifying anti-osteoporotic sterols from the soft coral Sclerophytum humesi .
items.summary: Marine soft corals represent a rich source of structurally diverse secondary metabolites; however, their potential effects on bone metabolism remain poorly explored. In this study, an integrated molecular networking- and bioactivity-guided strategy was employed to identify potential anti-osteoporotic constituents from the soft coral Sclerophytum humesi. LC-MS/MS-based molecular networking was integrated with biological activity data to prioritize bioactivity-associated molecular families for targeted isolation. In a glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis zebrafish model, fraction SH-E3 exhibited a pronounced ability to restore impaired skeletal mineralization and was therefore prioritized for further chemical investigation. Targeted isolation of SH-E3 afforded one previously undescribed compound (1) together with eight known metabolites (3-10), including six sterols: ergosta-5,24(28)-dien-3-ol (5), ergosta-5,22-dien-3-ol (6), cholesterol (7), gorgosterol (8), (3 β )-33-norgorgost-5-en-3-ol (9), and ergost-5-en-3-ol (10).
items.author: Peng BR, Chen YS, Wang TM, Luu PV, Pham QV, Lai GY, Wang HW, Chen LY, Su JH, Lai KH, Le HG, Pham NT, Tran TN, Lee MH.

items.title: The Effects of Intra-Day Temperature Variability on Cause-Specific Mortality: A Time-Stratified Case-Crossover Study in Chongqing, China.
items.summary: Although temperature variability (TV) has been linked to an increased mortality risk, the independent effect of intra-day TV remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the association between intra-day TV exposure and cause-specific mortality in a Chinese population. We collected daily mortality data and meteorological variables from 2016 to 2022 in Jiulongpo District, Chongqing, China. A time-stratified case-crossover design combined with a conditional logistic regression model was used to assess the association between TV exposure and the risk of cause-specific mortality. A natural spline function was used to derive the exposure-response (E-R) relationship between intra-day TV and the percentage change in mortality risk.
items.author: Yin Z, Lan Y, Tang C, Li W, An X, Qiu C, Liang X, Liang F.

items.title: 6-min walk test reveals early physiological impairment in fibrotic interstitial lung diseases.
items.summary: Rationale Early prediction of lung function decline remains challenging in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and fibrotic interstitial lung diseases (ILDs). We evaluated whether oxygen desaturation during the 6-min walk test (6MWT) predicts forced vital capacity (FVC) decline and long-term outcomes. Methods We analysed data from two independent cohorts: the nationwide Japanese Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias (JIPS) Registry and an external IPF cohort (K-Junko Study). Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated for each 6MWT parameter to identify variables associated with FVC decline and to determine optimal thresholds. Sensitivity analyses were conducted using Fine-Gray models. The performance of the predictive model was assessed using calibration plots and the concordance index (C-index).
items.author: Ogura T, Okuda R, Kuwahira I, Nishikiori H, Chiba H, Takeda Y, Suda T, Fujisawa T, Abe M, Tomioka H, Sakamoto S, Zaizen Y, Ohkubo H, Yamauchi H, Kawamura T, Kimura M, Sakamoto K, Koga Y, Nishiyama O, Nakagawa H, Yatera K, Usui K, Matsushima H, Hashimoto D, Handa T, Kishaba T, Ichiyasu H, Oyamada Y, Matsuda T, Ishimoto H, Narumoto O, Nukiwa T, Kobayashi K, JIPS Registry collaborators, JIPS Registry collaborators .

items.title: New hemiaminal ether dihydropyrimidinones as CK1/CK2 inhibitors targeting α-synuclein in Parkinson's disease.
items.summary: This study aimed to develop new dihdropyrimidones based inhibitors to slow Parkinson's disease progression by targeting casein kinase CK1, CK2, and α-synuclein receptors. A series of hemiaminal ether-functionalized DHPMs (3a-3h) was synthesized through late-stage alkoxymethylation of dihydropyrimidones in high yields (up to 92%) and characterized by NMR and mass spectrometry. Initial screening of the synthesized compounds (3a-3h) through molecular docking predicted strong binding to CK1 (PDB: 6RCG, up to -8.9 kcal mol -1 ), CK2 (PDB: 3NSZ, up to -10.3 kcal mol -1 ), and potential to inhibit α-synuclein (ASN) aggregation in both native (3Q25) and mutant forms (1XQ8). Normal mode analysis (NMA) examined the structural flexibility of mutant α-synuclein (1XQ8), while docking analysis identified potential binding regions (C1-C5), including interactions involving Ser129.
items.author: Wakeel H, Munir S, Gondal HY, Cheema ZM, Muskan A, Malik I, Nisar M, Siddiqui H, Sultan SK.

items.title: Development and comparative pharmacokinetic evaluation of iodine-125- and fluorine-18-labelled analogues of 4-(benzo[ d ]thiazol-2-yl)phenylboronic acid for boron neutron capture therapy.
items.summary: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) requires accurate assessment of boron biodistribution to support treatment planning. Radiolabelled analogues of 4-(benzo[ d ]thiazol-2-yl)phenylboronic acid (BTPB) were developed to investigate how radiohalogen substitution influences in vivo distribution and to explore their potential for imaging BTPB-related distribution characteristics. The aryl boronic acid moiety of BTPB was replaced with iodine-125 through copper-mediated iododeboronation to generate [ 125 I]IPBT, or with fluorine-18 through copper-mediated nucleophilic radiofluorination to produce [ 18 F]FPBT. Iododeboronation afforded [ 125 I]IPBT with an isolated radiochemical yield of 28.39 ± 5.12%, whereas radiofluorination afforded [ 18 F]FPBT with a lower decay-corrected isolated yield of 3.10 ± 1.35%.
items.author: Im C, Zia MR, Bibi I, Kang KJ, Kim JY, Kim HY, Park JA.

items.title: White-light-driven irreversible photochromism for tamper-evident anti-counterfeiting.
items.summary: Fluorescent photochromic molecules are promising materials for high-security anti-counterfeiting and information encryption. However, their practical applications are hindered by two limitations: their UV-dependent photochromic behavior causes inevitable photobleaching and inconvenient operation, while their reversibility is vulnerable to replication and tampering. Herein, we designed and synthesized three donor-acceptor type diarylethenes by introducing aniline derivatives into 2,3-bis(2-methyl-1-benzothiophene-1,1-dioxide-3-yl)-thiophene. The absorption onset of the open isomers redshifted to ∼480 nm as the electron donating ability of the aniline derivatives increased, and red color closed isomers appeared in both solution and film states along with turn-on red fluorescence upon conventional white-light irradiation. Notably, the cycloreversion process is inhibited with a negligible quantum yield as low as 3.4 × 10 -6 in ethyl acetate due to the high activation energy barrier in the excited state.
items.author: Li L, Li H, Yang C, Peng K, Lei P, Du H, Li Y, Liu X, Ai Q, Hu X.

items.title: Hop-and-sink locomotion and escape in benthic copepods under localized suction flow.
items.summary: Benthic copepods inhabit complex boundary layers where flow varies rapidly, yet their sensory-motor responses to localized hydrodynamic signals remain poorly understood. We quantified the behavior of the harpacticoid Tigriopus californicus under no-flow and localized suction flow using 3D particle tracking velocimetry of both copepod trajectories and the surrounding flow. Copepods frequently entered the water column and maintained a hop-and-sink gait, spending ~40% of time jumping with peak speeds up to 68 mm s -1 . In the far field (>2 mm from the source), kinematic statistics were indistinguishable from no-flow controls and orientations were consistent with random swimming. In the near field, individuals performed directed escape jumps (mean 80.6 ± 17.9 mm s -1 ; max.
items.author: Kastinger M, Brizzolara S, Redaelli T, Holzner M.

items.title: Facile smartphone-assisted colorimetric detection of high-load Hg 2+ in industrial wastewater using a silica-supported ion-imprinted polymer.
items.summary: Conventional colorimetric Hg 2+ sensors primarily target trace-level detection, limiting their applicability to industrial wastewater containing elevated mercury concentrations. Herein, a silica-supported APTES-TEOS ion-imprinted polymer (SiO 2 @MIP) was developed for smartphone-assisted colorimetric detection of high-load Hg 2+ in industrial wastewater. The synthesized material was characterized using FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, and XPS, while Hg 2+ detection was evaluated using UV-vis spectrophotometry and the Photometrix smartphone application. The proposed method exhibited a working concentration range of 1 mM-100 mM, with adsorption saturation observed above approximately 12.5 mM and a strong logarithmic calibration relationship ( R 2 = 0.9878), a limit of quantification was calculated to be 1.35 mM.
items.author: Nhiem LT, Tue Nam PH, Nhung TT, Sang NT.

items.title: An integrated hydrometallurgical route for recycling SmCo magnets from production waste.
items.summary: Conventional hydrometallurgical processes for recycling waste SmCo magnets often require substantial reagent consumption and remain cost-intensive, particularly when solvent extraction is employed as a downstream separation step. In the present study, an integrated hydrometallurgical route was developed for the recovery of samarium, cobalt, and copper from SmCo magnet production scrap. More than 99% of samarium, cobalt and iron from the SmCo magnet scrap were leached with sulfuric acid, whereas copper remained in the leaching residue. Samarium was subsequently recovered selectively from the leachate as a high-purity sodium-samarium double sulfate using sodium sulfate as the precipitating agent. Importantly, we developed a selective iron removal step as an integral part of the flowsheet wherein the Fe(ii) present in the solution was oxidized to Fe(iii) using MnO 2 , followed by selective precipitation of Fe(iii), aided by MnO.
items.author: Héritier TM, Volga M, Jena A, Borra CR, Edouard MM, Venkatesan P.

Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.

items.summary: Declan Rice joins BBC Sport's Kelly Cates, Danny Murphy and Micah Richards to analyse how Arsenal earned their first Premier League victory at Liverpool in 14 years.

items.summary: Kimi Antonelli was a natural driver at the age of three, according to his dad. Here's how he developed to become the F1 champion at the age of 20.

items.summary: A magnitude 4.6 earthquake was recorded Mid-Indian Ridge. The event happened on 01 November 2026 at 22:22 UTC, at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.

items.title: Reconsidering the Mechanism of Proton Pump Inhibitor-Associated Fundic Gland Polyps: Absence of Re-enlargement during Potassium-Competitive Acid Blocker Therapy.
items.summary: Fundic gland polyps (FGPs) may enlarge during long-term proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy, potentially in association with acid suppression and hypergastrinemia. Potassium-competitive acid blockers (PCABs) provide potent and sustained acid suppression and may induce comparable or greater elevations in serum gastrin levels than PPIs. We report a case of FGPs in which regression was documented after changes in acid-suppressive therapy, with no subsequent re-enlargement during long-term use of PCABs. A woman in her 60s with gastroesophageal reflux disease developed progressive enlargement of FGPs during 7 years of rabeprazole therapy. Rabeprazole was discontinued because of marked redness of the enlarged FGPs and concern for possible bleeding and was replaced with an H2-receptor antagonist.
items.author: Misumi Y, Marumo T, Ban S, Nonaka K.

items.title: Circulating Plasma Adiposomes as a Partial Lipidomic Readout of Matched Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue: Implications for Interorgan Communication.
items.summary: Background Prior studies established adipose-derived extracellular vesicles, or adiposomes, as mediators of interorgan communication with lipidomic signatures linked to cardiometabolic health. Because adiposomes signal to distant organs via the circulation, we examined whether circulating adiposome lipidomes reflect matched subcutaneous adipose tissue adiposomes. Methods This cross-sectional paired lipidomic study included 22 subjects with matched circulating and subcutaneous adipose tissue adiposome samples. Untargeted lipidomics quantified 773 lipid features across 18 detected broad classes. Spearman correlation was the primary across-subject species-level metric; pooled and within-subject Pearson and Spearman correlations, principal component analysis, Bland-Altman analysis, class composition, and matched-versus-mismatched similarity were complementary measures. Additional analyses evaluated sex, cardiometabolic phenotypes, and focused species-clinical associations.

items.title: A Secure IoT-Blockchain Framework for Vaccine Cold-Chain Monitoring With Predictive Analytics.
items.summary: Objective The objective of this research is to design and test a framework for secure monitoring of a vaccine cold-chain with the help of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, blockchain-based provenance verification, and predictive analytics. Methods The architecture of PharmaChain IoT Vault is an integrated system comprising low-power IoT telemetry acquisition, secure Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT)-based communication, integrity verification using SHA-256, a permissioned blockchain infrastructure, off-chain telemetry storage, and a forecasting module for transformers. A real-world vaccine cold-chain logistics (VCL) dataset of 26,674 observations was used for experimental evaluation, spanning 30 vaccine batches, 12 monitoring sites, and multiple distribution steps.

items.title: Surgical Management of Pediatric Nodular Lymphocyte-Predominant Hodgkin's Lymphoma: A Systematic Review of Surgical Outcomes and Case Report.
items.summary: Introduction Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) is a rare subtype, representing 5% of Hodgkin lymphoma cases. It is distinguished by lymphocyte-predominant cells expressing CD20 and CD79a but not CD15 and CD30. Pediatric NLPHL affects primarily males aged 4-17, often presenting with localized lymphadenopathy and favorable outcomes. NLPHL's distinct pathology makes treatment optimization critical. Long-term risks of chemotherapy and radiotherapy have led to interest in surgical resection for low-risk, early-stage disease. The objective of this study is to systematically review the available literature describing surgical management of pediatric NLPHL and summarize reported outcomes following surgical resection. Methods We conducted a systematic review of studies on pediatric NLPHL with a focus on surgical resection.

items.title: Identification of a Novel KRAS::ETNK1 Fusion Transcript in a Myelodysplastic/Myeloproliferative Overlap Syndrome With Eosinophilia: A Case Report.
items.summary: This work describes, to our knowledge, the first reported case of a patient with an MDS/MPN overlap syndrome harboring a novel KRAS::ETNK1 fusion transcript. The disease initially presented with eosinophilia, megakaryocyte expansion, mast cell infiltration, and a background of typical MDS/MPN-associated mutations ( ASXL1 , TET2 , EZH2 , BCOR , and SETBP1 ). Following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, the fusion-bearing clone disappeared due to a chromosome 12p deletion, and the disease evolved into secondary AML with distinct molecular drivers (MYB, EP300, FAT1, and GATA2). This case provides new insights into rare genetic alterations in MDS/MPN, possible mechanisms of immune-mediated clonal selection after allogeneic stem cell transplantation, and the dynamics of leukemic evolution.

items.title: From ER and mitochondria to contact sites: integrated regulation of ferroptosis in cardiovascular diseases.
items.summary: Iron is a central regulator of cellular redox homeostasis, supporting essential physiological processes. Given its critical biological importance, iron homeostasis is tightly regulated at both the systemic and cellular levels. Ferroptosis is a metabolically regulated, iron-dependent form of cell death characterized by the accumulation of phospholipid hydroperoxides driven by iron-catalyzed redox reactions, ultimately leading to oxidative membrane damage. Accumulating evidence indicates that ferroptosis emerges from the coordinated activity of multiple subcellular organelles rather than from isolated pathways. In this context, the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria have recently been established as key regulators of ferroptotic signaling. Notably, mitochondria-associated membranes (MAMs), by spatially coordinating redox signaling and lipid peroxidation, calcium fluxes, mitochondrial metabolism and lipid remodeling, are increasingly recognized as central hubs within the ferroptotic cascade, acting as modulators of cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis and as key sites of its execution.

items.title: Differences in genetic diversity between early isolates of yellow fever virus genotypes.
items.summary: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is the prototypical member of the genus Orthoflavivirus and is responsible for the disease yellow fever. Phylogenetic studies show YFV can be characterized into seven genotypes (East Africa [EA], East and Central Africa [ECA], West Africa I [WAI], West Africa II [WAII], South America I [SAI], South America II [SAII], and Angola [ANG]). We used Next Generation Sequencing to investigate and compare the genetic diversity of the seven genotypes of YFV using early isolated strains of known passage history from a variety of collection years. Genetic diversity varied between the seven genotypes, with the ECA genotype being more diverse than EA and WAI genotypes, but not the WAII genotype.

items.title: ATP-independent entropy-driven dsRNA unwinding by DDX3X revealed by coarse-grained simulations and deep learning
items.summary: by Kang Wang, Chun-Lai Ren, Yu-Qiang Ma DEAD-box RNA helicases (DDXs) are traditionally known as ATP-dependent motors that unwind double-stranded RNA (dsRNA). Recent experiments, however, show that some DDXs promote dsRNA unwinding even in the absence of ATP, raising a fundamental question about the physical mechanism underlying ATP-independent strand separation. Here, we develop a minimal, physics-based coarse-grained RNA model and incorporate weak, specific interactions between DDX3X and dsRNA, revealing the inherently stochastic nature of unwinding events. The unwinding process must overcome an energy barrier, but thermal fluctuations and entropy gain provide a driving force for RNA remodeling. We identify that dsRNA separation proceeds through rare yet obligatory strand-displacing intermediates facilitated by DDX3X.

items.title: Coupled beta and high-frequency oscillations emerge from synchronized bursting in a minimal model of the parkinsonian subthalamic nucleus
items.summary: by Hiba Sheheitli, Luke A. Johnson, Jing Wang, Joshua E. Aman, Jerrold L. Vitek Local field potentials (LFPs) recorded from the subthalamic nucleus (STN) in Parkinson’s disease (PD) exhibit a distinctive multiscale spectral signature: exaggerated beta-band oscillations (13–30 Hz) coupled to high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, 200–400 Hz), with HFO amplitude being phase-locked to the beta cycle. This phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) has been identified as a promising biomarker of the parkinsonian state, yet no biophysical model has explained how it emerges, what determines the HFO frequency, or how HFOs can exist without beta modulation in the medicated STN. Here we show that a heterogeneous population of excitatory Izhikevich neurons with recurrent coupling produces three dynamical regimes: (i) asynchronous tonic firing, (ii) asynchronous bursting, in which neurons burst individually producing broadband HFO power but without coherent population-level PAC, and (iii) synchronous bursting, which gives rise to beta-HFO PAC.
items.author: Hiba Sheheitli, Luke A. Johnson, Jing Wang et al.

items.title: Ten simple rules for teaching practical AI to health data teams
items.summary: by Eric Just, Aik Choon Tan Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly entered the healthcare discourse, often framed through the lens of frontier models, generative systems, and transformative potential. Yet for many healthcare data teams, the practical path from curiosity to capability remains unclear. Concerns about data privacy, regulatory compliance, brittle systems, and misaligned expectations frequently stall progress before meaningful experimentation can begin. This paper presents ten simple rules for teaching practical AI to healthcare data teams, grounded in real-world data, privacy-first experimentation, and system-level thinking. Drawing on hands-on training experiences and existing educational and methodological literature, we argue that AI education in healthcare must prioritize workflows over models, systems over components, and institutional capability over isolated technical success.
items.author: Eric Just, Aik Choon Tan

items.title: Interpretable embeddings of speech explain and enhance the brain encoding performance of audio models
items.summary: by Riki Shimizu, Richard J. Antonello, Chandan Singh, Nima Mesgarani Speech foundation models (SFMs) are increasingly hailed as powerful computational models of human speech perception. However, since their representations are inherently black-box, it remains unclear what drives their alignment with brain responses. To remedy this, we built linear encoding models from six interpretable feature families: mel-spectrogram, Gabor filter bank features, speech presence, phonetic, syntactic, and semantic features, and contextualized embeddings from three state-of-the-art SFMs (Whisper, HuBERT, WavLM), quantifying electrocorticography (ECoG) response variance shared between feature classes. Variance-partitioning analyses revealed several key insights: First, the SFMs’ alignment with the brain can be mostly accounted for by their ability to learn and encode simple interpretable speech features.
items.author: Riki Shimizu, Richard J. Antonello, Chandan Singh et al.

items.title: Degeneracy in neuronal bifurcation landscapes: Equivalent bifurcation sequences across distinct parameter sets
items.summary: by Gianmarco Cafaro, Christophe Bernard, Meysam Hashemi, Damien Depannemaecker Degeneracy, the capacity of structurally distinct systems to achieve similar functions, is a fundamental property of living organisms, enabling adaptability and resilience. Neurons can maintain stable activity patterns despite substantial variability in ion channel expression, highlighting how different intrinsic configurations can produce equivalent electrophysiological behaviors. Previous studies have shown that neuronal activity emerges from the interaction between intrinsic membrane properties and ionic concentration dynamics. However, how degeneracy is organized within the dynamical landscape of neurons and how different degenerate configurations respond to external perturbations remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate how distinct biophysical parameter sets generate equivalent bifurcation sequences and how their resilience changes under ionic modulation.
items.author: Gianmarco Cafaro, Christophe Bernard, Meysam Hashemi et al.

items.title: Conditional-prevalence correction for liability-scale analyses of covariate-adjusted binary GWAS
items.summary: by Siyi Chen Adjustment for heritable covariates in genome-wide association studies of disease can induce collider bias, creating spurious genetic associations. Following bias correction, interpretation on the liability scale, which represents continuous disease susceptibility, requires an appropriate conversion from log odds. We derive this conversion under a Gaussian liability model for small genetic effects. The direct effect, excluding pathways through the adjusted covariates, and the collider-bias component share a common conversion factor. We characterize how this factor depends on variation in disease risk across covariate values and extend the derivation to case-control sampling. In simulations, the proposed conversion reduced the effect-size inflation associated with scaling based solely on disease prevalence.
items.author: Siyi Chen

items.title: kri-1/KRIT1 promotes innate immune and lipid homeostasis in the C. elegans intestine
items.summary: by Akshay Alaghatta, Samantha Y. Tse-Kang, Daniel P. Bollen, Khursheed A. Wani, Nicholas D. Peterson, Read Pukkila-Worley Animals must differentially allocate essential metabolic resources in response to changing environmental conditions to ensure reproductive success. For example, adult C. elegans coordinate innate immune defenses during infection and also allocate fat stores to the germline, each of which are required for evolutionary fitness. The genetic mechanisms that integrate resource allocation and host defenses in this context, however, are not fully understood. From a forward genetic screen for novel regulators of innate immune gene transcription, we identified kri-1 , the nematode homolog of human Krev interaction trapped protein KRIT1 .
items.author: Akshay Alaghatta, Samantha Y. Tse-Kang, Daniel P. Bollen et al.

items.title: High quality chromosomal genome assemblies of three human Plasmodium species directly from natural infections
items.summary: by Sunil Kumar Dogga, Jesse C. Rop, Alex Makunin, Fiona Teltscher, Damon-Lee Pointon, Ying Sims, Marcela Uliano-Silva, James Torrance, Thomas C. Mathers, Jonathan M. D. Wood, Sekou Sissoko, Antoine Dara, Dinkorma T. Ouologuem, Arthur M. Talman, Abdoulaye A. Djimdé, Mara K. N. Lawniczak Malaria, caused by mosquito-transmitted Plasmodium parasites, remains a major global health challenge. While P. falciparum accounts for most malaria deaths, the lesser-studied P. ovale spp. and P. malariae also contribute to disease burden across many endemic regions, typically causing milder but chronic infections. Here, we generated high quality, chromosome-level reference genomes for P. ovale wallikeri , P.

items.title: Functional dissection of conserved RNAi pathways in antiviral immunity of several hemipteran insects
items.summary: by Yan Zhang, Zhuang-Xin Ye, Qing-Lu Ma, Bi-Yun Wang, Ji-Chong Zhuo, Hai-Jian Huang, Chuan-Xi Zhang, Jian-Ping Chen, Jun-Min Li The small silencing RNA pathways are crucial post-transcriptional gene silencing mechanisms involved in antiviral defense, gene regulation, and transposon suppression. In insects, the three main pathways are the microRNA (miRNA), Piwi-interacting RNA (piRNA), and small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathways. While these pathways are well-studied in model insects like fruit flies and mosquitoes (Order: Diptera), their functions in non-model insects remain largely unexplored. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive functional screening of core RNAi-related genes in a hemipteran insect, the small brown planthopper ( Laodelphax striatellus ).
